journal_text: Checked my phone ten times on the bus this morning, each time hoping the calendar would magically clear itself. I’ve got two customer calls I still need to prep for, and my shift ran over because someone called in sick again. Had to text my ex about switching pick-up times this week since my manager wants me in early Thursday. Neither of us can really flex, so we’re both annoyed, but I guess that’s the routine now. My son’s school sent a reminder about a project due Friday, which I still haven’t found time to help him with. I keep thinking if I just mapped everything out better, I’d avoid this kind of pile-up, but every week is a new shuffle. Didn’t even have time for breakfast, just grabbed a coffee at the station. I need to call my mom back too, she left a message about visiting this weekend, but I honestly don’t know where to fit that in. Work pressure just keeps bleeding into everything else. I wish I could just pause things for an hour and actually get ahead, but that’s not how it works.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
I spent a chunk of today just trying to get my calendar under control. The lab meeting ran late, so I had to push back the time I was supposed to finish prepping samples, and now I’ve got a backlog that’s going to bleed into tomorrow. I’m still not sure if my supervisor noticed, but it feels like there’s always something slipping through the cracks. I kept glancing at my phone all afternoon, half-hoping someone from the group chat would suggest getting together, but nothing. It’s just me in this apartment, surrounded by sticky notes and half-packed moving boxes I never finished unpacking.

I keep telling myself to be patient, that eventually I’ll get a grip on both the research schedule and maybe even a social life. But it’s hard when every to-do list seems to get longer by the end of the day. Dinner was microwaved leftovers (again), and I’m pretty sure I forgot to email the data set to Dr. K. I’ll set a reminder for tomorrow, but I know I’ll wake up already feeling like I’m behind. I wonder if anyone else here ever feels this scattered, or if that’s just a me thing.

Tried to make some toast this morning but the bread was still frozen and I didn’t want to wait for it to thaw, so I just ate two cold slices with peanut butter while standing by the sink. I kept thinking about how different even breakfast feels here, like I haven’t quite figured out the rhythm of this new place yet. The apartment still smells like cardboard and paint, and every sound from the hallway makes me jump a little because I’m not used to the way everything echoes. 

Now I’m sitting in my car in the parking lot, watching people rush past on their way to work. I’m supposed to be at the gallery in 15 minutes but it feels weird to go in so early, like I’m intruding on someone else’s routine. I keep flipping through my sketchbook but nothing feels right, not sure if it’s the restlessness from moving or just the usual pre-work jitters. My mind keeps wandering between ideas for new pieces and wondering if I’ll ever feel like I belong here. I brought my paints in the trunk, thinking maybe after work I’ll try to find a spot by the river, just to see if being outside helps me settle. It’s not that I hate it here, it’s just that everything feels temporary, like I’m waiting for something to click. Still, I guess starting over is supposed to feel like this. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try a new route to work or actually unpack that last box in the kitchen. Just need to keep moving, even if it’s just small steps.

Feeling pretty neutral right now, just sitting in my car before heading in. The morning went as usual, nothing exciting, just the usual breakfast and out the door. I got here a little early again, which is sort of my habit lately, gives me time to breathe before class. I ran into Mark when I was locking up my bike and things felt a bit off between us. He barely nodded and kept walking, and I don’t really know what that’s about. Maybe I said something weird last week; I can’t even remember. I keep wondering if I should just ask him or let it go. Honestly, I wish I didn’t care so much about these little things, but I do notice them. I’m trying to stay focused on what I came here to do, but sometimes these social hiccups throw me. Today’s schedule is packed, so maybe that’s a good distraction. I’ve got a group project meeting later and I really hope it doesn’t get awkward. I always end up being the one who organizes everything, which is fine, but it feels like I’m carrying too much sometimes. Still, doing my best to keep things orderly, even if people are unpredictable. Might grab a quick snack before heading inside. Time to put on the student face and get through the day.

Just got off the phone with Jamie, trying to sync up schedules for next week. It’s always this weird mix of polite and tense, like neither of us wants to say the wrong thing but we’re both tired of trying to keep things smooth. I suggested Tuesday and Thursday for drop-offs, but she didn’t sound thrilled. Not sure if something’s going on or she’s just annoyed I couldn’t do Wednesday. I keep replaying what I said, wondering if I sounded too blunt or not clear enough. 

It’s kind of draining, honestly. I want us to work together for our kid, but it sometimes feels like we’re just trying not to piss each other off. Maybe I’m overthinking it. I know we both have other things going on, and it’s not always about me. Still, I catch myself getting defensive before anything even happens. I wish I knew if I’m handling this the right way. I keep telling myself to just keep it simple, focus on the calendar, don’t get into feelings, but that’s hard when things feel awkward. Maybe it’ll get easier over time. Or maybe I just need to stop worrying about being perfect at this.

Feeling a little worn out but mostly steady this afternoon. The bus ride home is noisy, as usual, but I’m glad for the predictable routine. I keep thinking about the conversation I had with Mark earlier. He seemed annoyed that I hadn’t picked up groceries yet, but honestly, I just couldn’t fit it in between my classes and the library shift. The list of things I’m supposed to do keeps getting longer, and sometimes I wonder if I’m letting the small stuff pile up just because I can’t juggle it all perfectly anymore.

I keep checking my phone to make sure I haven’t missed any messages about our group project or the bills. There’s still the rent to think about, and the electric bill is due soon, so I’m tracking every dollar. We had a tense moment about the budget last night, too. It didn’t really turn into an argument, but there’s definitely some friction. I keep reminding myself to stay patient and to remember that we’re both under pressure. I need to figure out a better way to organize the week’s errands and maybe talk to Mark when things are less hectic. For now, I’ll just try to get through the evening without dropping any more balls.

persona.life_context: caring for a parent, stretched thin

journal_text: Mom called out for me at 6:30 this morning, forgot where her slippers were again. Had to help her get dressed and fix a quick breakfast before rushing out. Dropped three resumes online in the car, phone kept freezing, had to restart it twice. Now I’m sitting in the parking lot, watching people hurry inside, trying to psych myself up to go in too (even though I don’t work here yet). Tired, but at least the sun’s out and it isn’t raining. My bag’s got a protein bar and a spare phone charger, just in case. Hoping today one of these leads finally turns into an interview. Wrote a reminder to call Mom’s doctor on my lunch break so I don’t forget again.

Feeling a bit wired but good as I finally got a chunk of work done on the living room couch. I was deep into responding to investor emails when my roommate came in, asking if I could move my call to another room tomorrow. He sounded a little tense about it, and I think I was pretty blunt in my reply. I didn’t mean to brush him off, but I was locked into my thoughts and just wanted to finish the thread I was on.

After he left the room, I started wondering if I’d been too sharp. It’s not easy juggling my own schedule with his, especially with all these calls cropping up at random times. We both work from home a lot, and even though we try to coordinate, it feels like someone is always compromising. I respect that he needs quiet for his work too, but sometimes I forget how my hyperfocus can make me less flexible in the moment.

I should probably check in and let him know I’m not upset, just overloaded. We’ve lived together long enough to work through this kind of thing, but I don’t want small misunderstandings to stack up. Maybe tomorrow we can sit down and hash out a better plan for sharing work spaces. It’s a bit of an ongoing negotiation, but I guess that’s just part of sharing a place at this stage in life.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text: Feeling a little scattered this afternoon, trying to get through my list of edits at my bedroom desk. I kept checking my phone, half-hoping for a text from someone I met at the book club last week, but nothing yet. The quiet in the apartment is both comforting and a little too much at times. I started drafting an article idea about moving to a new city, but halfway through I realized I was mostly just rambling about my own uncertainty. I want to be more productive and also make more connections, but I keep bouncing between those two goals and not making real headway with either. I did force myself to sign up for a local writing group meeting on Thursday. It’s probably a good step, even if I feel awkward. For now, I’ll try to wrap up the edits before dinner and maybe take a walk to clear my head.

Just finished brushing my teeth and tried to sneak past my brother’s room without waking him up. I ended up stepping on a creaky floorboard, of course, and he called out, asking if I was still working. I kind of mumbled something about being done for the night, but he knew I was lying. He started asking questions about the business again, saying he overheard Mom worrying to Dad about me never taking breaks. I wanted to explain that it’s not that I can’t stop, but that I feel like if I do, everything will fall apart or I’ll lose momentum.

It’s weird to have everyone so close, literally a few feet away, and still feel like they don’t really get why I’m pushing myself like this. I tried to tell my brother that it’s not just about making money or proving anything to anyone. But I don’t know if I’m convincing him or even myself. There’s this constant low-level anxiety that if I slow down, I’ll miss something important, or the whole thing will slip away. At the same time, I know I sound dramatic, and I can see why my family worries. But I also feel optimistic that something good is coming if I just keep at it.

I wish I could talk more openly about the uncertainty I feel, but I always end up holding back. Maybe I’m afraid they’ll think I’m not as sure of myself as I pretend to be. Or maybe I just don’t want their worry to get worse. Either way, tonight’s conversation left me a bit unsettled. I want them to trust me, but I’m not sure if I even trust myself right now.

The early sun glare is bouncing off the neighbor’s window right onto my desk, lighting up the clutter in a way that makes it all look even more chaotic. I’m running on maybe four hours of sleep and my brain feels like it’s moving through syrup, but I keep replaying that conversation with Josh from this morning. He stopped by before work, apparently just to “check in,” but the way he kept glancing at my empty wallet on the desk, I could tell he wanted to say something about my situation. I tried to keep things light, tossed out a sarcastic comment about my new minimalist lifestyle, but I’m not sure he picked up on it. Sometimes I wonder if my dry humor just flies right over people’s heads or if I’m unconsciously using it to keep things at arm’s length.

I know he means well, and maybe I’m reading into things because I’m tired and stressed, but it felt like he was judging me a little. Or maybe I was the one judging myself and projecting it onto him. Either way, the whole thing left me feeling a bit raw. I don’t like talking about money, especially when things are tight. Part of me wants to reach out later and clarify, but the other part just wants to let it go and hope it didn’t come off as awkward as it felt. Social stuff always feels trickier when I’m running on empty. I need to remember that not every interaction is a referendum on my life decisions, but it’s hard not to get defensive when things are this precarious. At least in here, behind the closed door, I can just breathe and be irritated in peace.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
Birds were pretty loud this morning, walking down the block, and I kept thinking about all the things I still haven’t crossed off. My phone kept buzzing in my pocket, work slack and school reminders mixing together. I’m so behind on the group project, barely time to read the assignment last night after pushing a patch at 9pm. Not sure if it’s better to finish the bug fix or just start the homework first, both are due soon and feel equally urgent.

Didn’t pack lunch again, so I’ll have to pick something up between meetings, if there’s time. My brain is foggy and my to-do list is a mess. I keep telling myself to prioritize but everything blurs together lately. Maybe tonight I’ll finally block out an hour just to re-organize all the deadlines and see if I can actually catch up.

Just finished washing the dishes after dinner, and I couldn’t help running through all the little things still left on my to-do list. The kitchen was quiet except for the hum of the fridge, and I kept glancing at my phone, feeling like I was supposed to answer more emails or check on a client ticket. Work feels overwhelming lately, like it’s all coming at me at once and I’m not moving fast enough to keep up.

I keep wondering if I’m actually building something with this freelancing, or if I’m just spinning my wheels. There was a moment earlier today when I was on a call with a customer and I caught myself zoning out, thinking about whether I should look for something more stable. The idea of change is both terrifying and kind of exciting. Income has been so hit or miss this month, and it’s hard not to worry about next week’s bills. But I also know that I value the independence. I don’t want to give that up unless I have to.

Tonight I felt the anxiety in my chest again, especially when I looked at my calendar and realized how many deadlines I’d squeezed into the next few days. I know I need to slow down and breathe, but it always feels like there’s just one more thing to do. Maybe I’ll take a walk tomorrow morning, just to clear my head. I want to feel more grounded, not just constantly reacting to whatever task pops up next.

The fridge is humming louder than usual and the hallway light is the only thing on. I can't sleep, brain spinning with every little thing I didn't get done today. Had to switch up the kids' pick-up again because Jordan's meeting ran late, and I could see the disappointment on Eli's face when I was late. That stuck with me all day. I keep replaying that moment, wondering if I could have planned it better, if I'm screwing this up more than helping. It's so tiring to juggle everything, calendars and texts and reminders, and still feel like I'm missing the most important parts. Tonight, after they were asleep, I sat on the couch and just felt this huge ache. Missing the old rhythm, the way things used to be before all the splitting and lists and extra steps. I keep telling myself it's just a phase, but it feels so heavy sometimes. I want to be better at this, but I don't know what better even looks like right now. The silence isn't helping. I just wish I could make it all smoother for them, and for me.

The bus is rattling along and the overhead lights are flickering every time we hit a bump, which is oddly fitting because my brain feels just as jumpy. I keep thinking about whether I remembered to put my roommate's package inside the apartment or if it's still sitting by the door (she’ll let me know soon enough, I guess). My phone vibrated with a calendar reminder for the third time today and I still haven’t figured out how I’m supposed to get to that dentist appointment on Friday without messing up the office filing. There’s a pile of sticky notes in my bag, each one with a different color and a different unfinished task, but right now I can’t even remember which color is for groceries and which is for work errands.

I’m trying not to make eye contact with anyone because I can’t really handle small talk tonight. I also have to remember to check if my laundry finished or if my roommate needed the washer, and if I don’t get the rent payment sent before midnight, the landlord will start in with the passive-aggressive texts again. The bus smells vaguely of burnt rubber and someone’s takeout, which is making me hungry and annoyed at the same time. I wish I could just hit pause for a second and make a list that stays made for more than five minutes, but, knowing me, I’ll just rewrite it tomorrow. Maybe I’ll finally get through the day without forgetting something obvious, but I’m not holding my breath.

My feet are tucked under the scratchy old blanket on the couch, and every time I shift, it bunches up in a weird way. The apartment is quiet for once, just the hum of the fridge and the soft traffic outside, but my mind is still racing. I tried to organize the shared calendar again tonight, but someone keeps adding things without telling me, and I’m starting to feel like I live in a puzzle where the pieces keep changing. I keep thinking about what I’m supposed to do next now that I’m not working. Part of me is hopeful that this is just a weird in-between moment, but I also feel kind of lost, like I’m waiting for a signal that probably isn’t coming. It’s exhausting to keep acting like everything is fine with my roommates when I don’t even know how to answer when people ask what I do all day. I did manage to cook dinner (spaghetti again, because it’s easy and nobody complains), and afterward, I sorted old receipts into neat piles, which made me feel a little more in control. Sometimes I wonder if all this organizing is just a way to distract myself from the fact that I don’t know who I am right now. I keep thinking about signing up for something new, maybe a class or volunteering, but I haven’t actually done it yet. The living room light is too bright and I should get up to turn it off, but I just keep sitting here, thinking that maybe tomorrow will feel less confusing. I know I can figure this out eventually, but tonight everything feels a bit too much. Still, I made it through today, and I guess that counts for something. 😊

I spent most of the afternoon walking around the block, trying to mentally sort out the pile of family logistics that have been building up since the move. The new school registration papers are still sitting on the kitchen table, untouched, and I keep forgetting to call the pediatrician to transfer records. It’s embarrassing how many things are half-finished, like the insurance forms that I start and then lose in the shuffle, or forgetting to update Mom’s contact at the pharmacy. My phone buzzed twice while I was out, both times reminders about appointments I set and then almost instantly forgot about. I keep thinking if I just write everything down in one place I’ll get ahead of it, but I end up with sticky notes everywhere and still feel like I’m missing something important.

I noticed how tense my shoulders were as I walked, probably from sitting at the computer too long and not really getting anywhere with work either. The guilt is there, creeping in every time I catch myself daydreaming or just staring out the window instead of actually calling people back. It’s like I’m juggling all these small but urgent things and not doing any of them well, which is honestly frustrating. I wish I could just pause everything for a day and map out what needs to be done, but I know that’s not how life works. Maybe after dinner I’ll try to organize the paperwork again, or at least set a timer so I don’t get sidetracked. The thought of another week like this makes me feel tired, but I guess I just have to keep chipping away at the list.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text: Had to finish the mockup for the group project, but my laptop was being really slow again. I ended up sitting at the kitchen table around midnight, with my sketchbook and three different color pens, trying to map out what I actually wanted this thing to look like. I keep telling myself I’m a designer, but lately it feels more like I’m just barely holding the pieces together. My roommate stumbled in and asked if I was ever going to sleep, and I laughed it off, but it did make me wonder if I’m getting too wrapped up in all this. I do like the challenge. It’s what got me into design in the first place, solving little puzzles and making things work. But I keep getting this nagging feeling that I’m faking it somehow, like everyone else has it figured out and I’m just doodling in the margins. Still, I finished the wireframe, and I even kind of like it. I guess it’s weird to feel proud and unsure at the same time. Maybe that’s just how it goes when you’re trying to become someone. Anyway, left the pens out. I’ll deal with them in the morning. For now, just glad I made progress, even if it’s small.

Sunlight is coming in through the blinds and hitting the coffee table in weird stripes, and I can hear the washing machine rumbling in the next room. I got home from work about an hour ago and my legs are still sore from running around picking orders all day. There was a big shipment in the morning, so we were all hustling, and it felt like I barely had a second to breathe. Lunch was basically a granola bar at my locker because the line in the break room was too long. I keep thinking about the dumb argument we had this morning before I left for work, and I want to talk about it but I’m exhausted and worried I’ll make things worse. I know we both want to get better at talking things out, but it’s so hard when we’re both tired and stressed. For now, I’m just sitting here, listening to the washer and trying to slow down before I start dinner.

The mug is still warm in my hands, and I keep glancing at my phone every couple of minutes. Sitting in this cramped coffee shop corner, I’m trying to piece together the rest of my day between sips. I need to send out two client proposals before lunch, but my mind keeps drifting to tonight’s school meeting and whether I remembered to sign the permission slip that was due this morning.

My planner is a mess of scribbles, sticky notes, and half-finished lists. Between freelance deadlines, grocery runs, and making sure dinner is something besides cereal, I feel like I’m always one step behind. The sitter texted earlier to say she’s only available until four, which means I’ll have to reschedule a Zoom call, again. There’s laundry waiting at home, and I still haven’t figured out how to fit in a quick grocery run before the kids are home.

I can’t decide if I’m being productive or just spinning my wheels. There’s a weird comfort in the noise around me, even as I try to focus. I keep telling myself I’ll get a better handle on all this, but for now I just need to get through today’s list without forgetting anything crucial. Maybe tonight, after the house is quiet, I’ll actually check something off for good.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
My feet are still sore from standing behind the counter all day. I’m sitting on the edge of my bed, staring at the half-unpacked boxes stacked in the corner. I keep telling myself I’ll finish sorting them on my next day off, but I never seem to get around to it. Moving here was supposed to shake things up, but late at night the apartment still feels unfamiliar. Today a customer asked if I was from around here, and I hesitated before saying yes. I guess I don’t know what counts as being from anywhere anymore.

After work, I walked a few blocks out of my way just to avoid the busy intersections. It’s like I’m looking for something but I don’t even know what that is. I caught my reflection in a shop window and didn’t quite recognize myself. There’s this constant urge to figure out where I fit in, but most days I’m just focused on getting through the shift and not overanalyzing every small interaction. I try to stay optimistic, but sometimes I wonder if I’m just waiting for something to happen instead of making it happen. Maybe that’s why I keep replaying every conversation in my head. I know I should reach out more, try harder to build connections, but it’s easier to just come home and let the TV fill the silence. Still, I find myself hoping that tomorrow I’ll feel a little more settled, or at least a little less like I’m drifting.

There’s a constant low chatter in this coffee shop corner, cups clinking and the occasional hiss from the espresso machine. I picked this seat hoping for a moment to sort myself out after another long day at the new school. I keep replaying the conversation I had with Clara, one of the other teachers. She asked if I’m settling in and I said yes, but it didn’t sound convincing to either of us. I wonder if she picked up on how uncertain I feel or if she was just making small talk. We talked about lesson planning and classroom management, but I couldn’t shake the feeling that I was on the outside of some invisible circle. Maybe that’s just something that takes time, or maybe I’m not doing enough to connect. It’s confusing, not knowing if I’m supposed to push myself into these new relationships or just let them happen. There’s a part of me that wants to stay quiet, observe, and figure out the dynamics before I say too much. I know I’m a private person, but I also want to belong. I left the conversation feeling both relieved it was over and annoyed at myself for not being more open. There’s this nagging feeling that I’m missing some step in how to build a life here. I keep telling myself I’ll feel grounded eventually, but right now it’s like I’m watching everything from the side, waiting for the moment when it feels real.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text: This morning when I was putting on my shoes, I remembered how my mom used to always tell me to double knot the laces so I wouldn’t trip. That popped in my head out of nowhere. I walked around the block before work, mostly just to clear my head. The air felt weirdly heavy, maybe just humidity or maybe I’m just tired. Saw a neighbor walking their dog and waved. I realized I still haven’t called my sister back about Dad’s appointment. I know I should, but I keep putting it off and then I feel guilty. Thinking about it, I don’t really know where things are going with Jake. He texted late last night but I didn’t answer. I can’t tell if I just need space or if I’m avoiding something. There’s so much uncertainty right now and I don’t feel like myself, but I also don’t know what ‘myself’ even is most days. I guess I’ll try to check in with Dad later. Work is waiting and I have to focus, but it feels impossible today.

I just finished dinner and I’m still thinking about that call with my brother earlier. He asked if I could help him organize some stuff for Mom’s birthday, which honestly sounded doable, but then he kept adding on more things. I kept nodding along even though my mind was all over the place, and now I’m not sure what I actually agreed to or if I missed some important details. It’s so hard to pay attention lately, especially when I’ve been staring at a screen all day for school and work. There’s no real line between when I’m supposed to be working or relaxing, and I think I let that spill into my conversation with him. I want to be helpful, but I also feel annoyed that I can’t just say no or set boundaries. Was I being too passive? Or maybe he just assumes I have more time because I’m home so much. I can’t tell if I’m making this into a bigger deal than it is. Either way, I need to sort out what I actually need to do for this birthday plan, or I’m going to forget something important. My brain feels like it’s packed with half-finished lists.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
Had to clear my head this afternoon, so I took a walk around the block after getting another job rejection. My phone buzzed with a text from Jason, which caught me off guard. We haven’t really talked since that weird argument last week. He said he wanted to talk things out and maybe meet up, but I couldn’t tell if he was actually sorry or just wanted to smooth things over to avoid more awkwardness in the group. Honestly, I’m not sure if I overreacted to what he said, or if I’m right to still be annoyed. It’s been bothering me more than I want to admit, especially since I don’t have a ton of friends here yet.

I kept replaying the conversation in my head as I walked past the same row of empty storefronts. Part of me wants to just move on and forget it, but another part keeps poking at it, wondering if I messed up or if it’s a sign that we’re not really on the same page. I keep thinking about what I should say if we meet up. Should I just be direct and tell him it hurt, or is that making a bigger deal out of things? My anxiety makes me second-guess everything lately, even simple stuff like whether to send a quick reply or wait until I feel less tired. 

By the time I got back to my apartment, I felt a little better, but still unsure. Maybe it’s worth trying to fix things, even if it’s awkward. I do want to feel like I belong here, and keeping things bottled up hasn’t really helped. I’ll probably text him back later tonight. For now, I just needed to write it out and try to get some perspective. Not sure what’s right, but at least I’m thinking about it.

This morning I remembered walking past the kitchen table and seeing Mom’s old planner sitting there, still open to last week. It made me pause for a second, thinking about how much she used to write in it and how I always thought her color-coded notes were overkill. Now I wish I had that kind of structure because lately my head feels like a spinning top, especially since moving here. The kitchen feels too big and empty this morning, with only the hum of the fridge and the weird ticking sound the clock makes.

I keep trying to write out a new schedule for myself and for the house stuff but all I’ve done is scribble half-formed to-do lists. There’s the grocery run I was supposed to do yesterday, the calls we need to make about Dad's next appointment, and I still haven’t found the right box with the insurance papers. I keep thinking I’ll sort out the bathroom closet too, but I just open the door and close it again. It’s like the more I try to get organized, the more things I remember I haven’t done. I know I said I’d help with meals this week but I’m not even sure what’s in the freezer anymore. I think my sister expects me to just know what needs to be done, but half the time I can’t even remember where we put the extra towels.

There’s a sticky note on the fridge with a reminder about a prescription pickup, and I’m afraid I’ll forget that too. I wish I could just wake up and have a plan, or a list that actually makes sense and isn’t just a bunch of half-finished thoughts. I guess I’m supposed to be the responsible one now, but it doesn’t feel real yet. Maybe I’ll try to make a new list after breakfast, or maybe I’ll just stare at the planner again and hope something clicks. I know things will settle eventually, but right now it’s just a lot all at once.

The hum of the refrigerator is louder than usual in the kitchen at lunch. Sunlight is coming through the blinds, catching on the pile of invoices I still haven’t sorted. It’s quiet enough that I can hear my own chewing, which makes me oddly self-conscious.

This morning, I called Mom to check in, like I do most days. She sounded tired, but insisted she was fine. There’s a strain in her voice lately that she tries to hide. I can tell she’s still struggling after Dad’s funeral, even though we don’t talk about it directly. I wanted to say something comforting, but the words stuck. Instead, I just asked if she needed groceries, and she said no, as usual. It’s frustrating not knowing how to help, or if I’m even helping at all.

Remote work makes it too easy to stay in my own head. I keep thinking I should drive over to see her, but the days blur together, and by evening I’m too drained. I keep replaying that last conversation I had with Dad in the hospital, wondering if I missed something important. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try again with Mom, just sit and listen. That feels like the only thing I can do right now.

Left the apartment in a rush this morning. My partner and I barely spoke, just a few words about bills and who’s picking up groceries. I kept thinking about that moment the whole drive over, trying to remember if I’d checked the fridge for leftovers for lunch. Now I’m sitting in the parking lot, early, but too tired to even close my eyes for a minute.

We’re supposed to sit down tonight and go over the budget again, but I know it’s going to be tense. Money’s tight and every little thing feels bigger than it is. I keep replaying our conversations, wondering if I missed something or should have said less. Work starts soon and I still haven’t figured out when to pick up the prescription or if I can squeeze in laundry. My mind keeps jumping from one thing to another. I want things to feel easier between us, but today it just feels like too much at once.

Missed the last bus by three minutes tonight and had to wait in the weird fluorescent light with that sticky feeling of being overtired, but when I finally got on and found a seat by the window, something shifted. I was thinking about all the deadlines piling up (the blog edits, the pitch that still sounds fake to me, the emails I haven’t answered), and then this kid got on the bus with this huge ridiculous rainbow scarf, like he didn’t care at all what anyone thought. He was humming, totally off-key, and for some reason it made me smile even though I was trying not to. I keep wondering if I ever had that kind of confidence or if I ever will. Sometimes remote work feels like I’m always halfway in my job and halfway out, like my whole identity is smeared between Slack notifications and trying to remember to eat lunch before 5pm. I know I’m supposed to be grateful for the flexibility and not commuting every day, but lately, I miss the messy boundaries. At least then, I felt like I knew where work ended and real life started. Today I spent hours organizing my notes for a story idea, but I still don’t know if it’s any good or if I’m just going through the motions. Maybe that’s why seeing someone just own their space felt so sharp and strange. I keep telling myself I’ll figure it out, but tonight I really felt the weight of not being sure who I am outside of work, or even inside of it. Maybe tomorrow will feel more solid, or at least less confusing. For now, I just want to get home, eat something easy, and maybe let myself be a little aimless, just for a while.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text: My legs are cramped against the seat in front of me and I can hear some teenager’s music leaking out of their headphones a few rows back. The bus smells like wet jackets and old air, which isn’t my favorite, but I’m too tired to care today. I kept thinking about last night’s argument with Sam when I was supposed to be listening to a podcast. It wasn’t a huge fight, but I keep replaying how blunt I got when we talked about meeting each other’s kids. I feel like I’m stumbling around in the dark with this whole new relationship thing. I like them, but the idea of blending our lives just feels messy and unpredictable. Maybe I’m overthinking it, or maybe I’m just not ready to let someone else into the chaos of my daily routine. Parenting takes up so much space in my head, and I’m not sure where a new person fits yet. Still, I caught myself smiling at a text from them earlier, so clearly I’m not ready to walk away either. The city outside the window looks washed out, but there’s a weird comfort in watching everyone else go about their afternoons. I’ll probably order takeout and let the kid pick the movie tonight. Not in the mood for deep talks or big decisions. Sometimes the best I can do is just get us both home in one piece and see what tomorrow feels like.

Feeling pretty worn out this afternoon, sitting at my desk and trying to sort through the mountain of emails and Slack messages that piled up while I was in meetings. I had to juggle three different client calls today, all of them with their own set of shifting deadlines and last-minute requests. The unpredictability of freelancing can be a headache, especially on weeks like this when the money’s not guaranteed and everyone wants answers at once. I tried to keep my project board updated, but it’s starting to look like a crime scene with all the overdue tasks marked in red. My phone buzzed nonstop while I was trying to get a contract updated for one client, and that made it almost impossible to focus.

On top of the work chaos, there’s been tension at home. Had a short, clipped conversation with my partner about who’s picking up groceries and handling the laundry. Neither of us is really sleeping enough lately, and it’s making every small thing feel like a big deal. We keep circling the same arguments about time management and who’s pulling more weight, which never feels productive. I know I’m not giving her my full attention, but it’s hard when my head’s spinning with a dozen logistical problems. I told myself I’d try to carve out some time for us this weekend, but even that feels like another item on the endless to-do list. Maybe things will ease up once I clear a few projects, but right now it just feels like I’m treading water. At least the cat is happy to have me stuck at the desk all day. Not sure if that counts as a win, but I’ll take what I can get.

Feeling kind of neutral this morning. I sat at my desk texting Riley about drop-off for the week and somehow we ended up talking in circles. I thought Wednesday was my turn but she swears she mentioned a switch last week. Honestly, I can't remember and my calendar is a mess. It's so frustrating trying to keep things straight when we're both busy and tired.

I want to keep things smooth for our kid, but sometimes I wonder if we're actually making it harder by always trying to be flexible. I probably should have just called instead of texting, but I didn't want to wake anyone up. Now I'm just hoping we didn't both double book. Guess I'll figure it out later today.

Put my phone down after texting Alex about the groceries. I thought it was my turn, but the way he replied, maybe he assumed he was supposed to do it. We always end up circling around these small things, making them feel bigger than they are. I don’t know if it’s just the way I phrase things or if he’s actually annoyed. It’s weird because I try to be clear, but sometimes I worry I sound too blunt. Sitting on the couch now, listening to the fridge hum, I’m thinking about how much I overthink these small roommate interactions. I want to be easy to live with, but I also can’t help wanting things done a certain way, especially with our clashing schedules. The kitchen feels like neutral ground most days, but every now and then, it gets tense. Maybe I should just ask directly next time or let it go. Not sure which is better. I don’t want to make things awkward, but I also don’t want to keep guessing. Sometimes being gentle feels like tiptoeing. For now, I’ll let it settle and see how it feels in the morning.

Just put the last load of dishes in the dishwasher and flopped on the couch, which I’ve been looking forward to since this morning. The day was nonstop from the moment my alarm buzzed (which I snoozed twice, ugh) to dashing out the door with half my hair done and then classes that somehow felt longer than usual. After class, I had to coordinate with him about who’s got which days this week, and for some reason, even after all this time, it still gets tense. We both try to be reasonable but tonight I snapped a little and now I feel bad. Maybe it’s just how tired I am or maybe I’m frustrated that my planner never seems big enough for everything. I keep promising myself I’ll be more on top of things, but then suddenly it’s 10 pm again. 

I know we’re both juggling a lot, but I wish it didn’t always feel like a negotiation. Still, even with the calendar mess and the awkward silences, we did end up laughing about how neither of us can remember which backpack has the homework folder. I guess that’s something. I’m grateful we can still joke, even after the little arguments. There’s still a lot to figure out and I’m so tired my brain is fuzzy, but I think we’ll manage. For now, I’m just going to enjoy five minutes of quiet before I have to check if the laundry actually dried or if I’ll be waking up to damp socks again.

I felt a little unsettled tonight as I walked around the block after dinner. The air had cooled down, which made the houses seem quieter than usual, and it gave me some space to think about Mom. It's been months since her diagnosis, but it still catches me off guard when I remember how quickly things changed. I keep noticing small things she liked, like the smell from that jasmine bush near the corner, and it makes me pause. Sometimes I worry that if I get too locked into my routines, I’ll miss these details, but at the same time, having structure helps me manage the restlessness.

I tried sketching a bit earlier, but my mind kept wandering back to the family group chat and the updates about her next doctor’s visit. I want to be hopeful for her, but I can’t help running through possible outcomes in my head. I wonder if my organized streak is actually helping anyone, or if it just gives me something to do so I don’t have to sit with all the uncertainty. I’m grateful for the quiet tonight, though. It’s easier to listen to what I’m actually feeling when the world slows down a bit.

Earlier today, I was halfway through a video lecture when my phone buzzed with a reminder about a freelance deadline I’d forgotten. I paused the video, went to jot down a plan, then realized I hadn’t finished my notes from yesterday. Now, sitting here on my lunch break, the quiet should be calming, but my brain keeps replaying all the little things I haven’t managed yet. There’s that research project due next week, a client waiting for edits, and I still need to schedule a meeting with my advisor. I thought freelancing would feel freeing, but mostly I feel like I’m spinning plates, hoping none of them crash. My calendar is a mess of scribbles and rescheduled tasks. I’m trying to keep my energy up with some leftovers and a sad apple, but it’s hard to focus on eating when my mind is darting between responsibilities. Sometimes I wonder if I’m actually getting anywhere, or just moving things around. Maybe I’ll figure out a better system, but right now it feels like I’m just treading water. At least I remembered to eat lunch today, so that’s something.

The toaster is still broken, so I had to use the oven to make toast. I stood there waiting, looking at the stack of dishes from last night. There’s a draft coming in from the kitchen window. I wrote out a list of things I have to do before this afternoon: pick up my finished canvas from the studio, call the gallery about the hanging schedule, and figure out how to coordinate groceries without another argument. I keep thinking about last night’s conversation. We got stuck trying to decide who was doing what this week. It turned into a small argument over who last bought groceries and who still needed to pick up supplies for the house. It would help if we just wrote everything down, but we never seem to stick to that for more than a few days at a time.

The kitchen table is covered in receipts and half-finished sketches. I can’t focus on the creative stuff until I clear at least some of the mess. This afternoon is going to be tight for time. After the studio, I have to fit in a call with a client who keeps changing her mind about colors. I should probably prep dinner in advance, but I don’t even know what we have left in the fridge. I’m hyperfocused on getting the schedule to work but there are too many moving parts. The microwave beeped and I realized I reheated the same cup of tea twice. I need to leave a note for her about the groceries before I forget. At least the toast turned out okay.

My sandwich is getting soggy on the edge where I left it too close to my water bottle. I keep staring at it instead of eating, feeling the weight of the quiet in the staff lounge. The hospital feels even bigger since I moved here. I thought being busy would help, but all the new faces and routines just make me miss home more.

Today a patient’s mother grabbed my hand. Her eyes were red, and she didn’t say much, just squeezed and let go. I’ve seen grief before, but it hit differently this time. Maybe because I’m the one feeling a little lost too.

I keep thinking about my own mom, how she’d always know what to say when things felt heavy. Now I can’t call her, so I just sit here, pretending the food tastes normal.

The quiet is louder than usual this afternoon. I wish I could shake this restless energy, but I just keep counting down minutes until my shift ends, hoping tomorrow feels less hollow.

The bus smells faintly of wet umbrellas and overheated electronics. My laptop bag is digging into my side, and I keep checking my phone, even though there aren't any urgent emails. I should feel relieved that another long day is over, but mostly I just feel unsettled. Spent part of the afternoon on a video call with the team, trying to motivate everyone, but I could tell my words were landing flat. It bothers me that I can't tell if it's them, or just my own fatigue coloring everything. 

There was a moment when someone asked why we were pushing so hard on this new feature, and I nearly snapped. Instead, I mumbled something about vision and impact, but I didn't really believe myself. It's starting to feel like I'm just moving pieces around, not building towards anything solid. The line between work and the rest of my life is so thin now that I don't know which part of me is actually running the show. All I want tonight is to go home and not think about any of this, but I know I'll probably open my laptop again after dinner. Maybe that's just how things are now.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text: Trying to sort out my week tonight and already feeling a bit lost in the shuffle. There’s a stack of bills on the coffee table that I need to look at, but I keep putting it off. Work at the shop was solid today, lots of oil changes and a couple of brake jobs, but the manager asked if I could pick up a Saturday shift. I said yes before really thinking about what I had to move around. That means I’ll have to reschedule the grocery run and probably laundry too. It’s weird not having anyone to split errands with, especially here where everything still feels new and I don’t have anyone to call for a quick favor. I was hoping to check out that trivia night down the street with some of the guys from work, but now I’m not sure if I’ll have the energy. My head’s kind of cloudy, but I keep telling myself it’ll settle down once I actually get into a routine. For now, I just have to remember to pick up dog food tomorrow and maybe finally unpack the last box by the door. Not glamorous, but at least everything’s moving forward, even if a bit out of order.

Needed to figure out how to swap my early shift with Mike but he never got back to me, so everything is still up in the air for tomorrow. Walked around the block late last night just to clear my head after arguing with Jen about the trash schedule again. She says I’m not pulling my weight, but I’m the only one who’s kept the kitchen from turning into a disaster. Feels like I’m the only one checking the calendar and making sure bills are lined up, but somehow I’m still the bad guy when something slips. I’m tired, not just from work but from trying to keep this place running smoothly when no one else seems to care. The walk helped a bit, but all I could think about was the pile of laundry waiting and whether I remembered to pick up dish soap. I know I’m not easy to live with, but it shouldn’t always be this hard to just get through the week. Wish I could just focus on one thing at a time instead of feeling like I’m juggling everyone’s messes. Maybe tomorrow will be better if I can just get some sleep and catch up on the stuff I missed.

The soft glow from my desk lamp is hitting the pile of patient charts I need to update, but the room is quiet except for the occasional car outside. Today was one of those days where I thought about money more than I wanted to. Freelancing as a nurse is a weird mix of freedom and anxiety. I got called in last minute to cover a shift at a new clinic, and it actually went better than I expected. There was a woman who came in really nervous about her blood pressure, and I could tell she just needed someone to listen. I took a few extra minutes to talk with her, even though I was technically already behind. She left smiling, and it honestly made my whole afternoon. I keep wondering if I should be hustling harder to line up more work, but moments like that remind me why I do this. Still, I can't ignore the nagging thought about what next week's paycheck will look like. I'm grateful for the flexibility, but I'm tired just thinking about the unpredictability. Right now, I just want to enjoy the quiet and not overthink everything for five minutes.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text: My desk lamp is flickering again, even though I just tightened the bulb last week. I was sitting here last night, trying to finish a paper, when Jamie texted asking if we could talk. He’s been weird with me since I missed the group meetup, and I guess I get it, but I’m already drowning in work and the kiddo had a meltdown right before bedtime. I tried explaining, but honestly, I don’t think he got it. Or maybe I didn’t explain it well. My brain was foggy and I ended up just apologizing over and over, which felt lame. I keep replaying the conversation, wondering if I should have said something different, like actually told him how overwhelmed I am, but then I think maybe that’s just over-sharing. It’s hard to know when to be honest or just keep it short and move on. Now I’m sitting here with my book open and nothing sinking in, just thinking about how annoying it is to feel like I’m letting people down, even when I’m doing my best. Why does it feel like being a good friend and a decent dad are on opposite teams sometimes? Anyway, my head hurts and I’m too tired to figure it out tonight.

Laptop is open, receipts spread out all over the desk. I’m trying to figure out if I can squeeze another week before needing to buy groceries again. The numbers aren’t adding up the way I hoped, but maybe if I lay off the snacks at work, I can make it work. Had a long shift today, too many customers asking where things are when the shelves are a mess. Not sure if I’m keeping up with the store’s new inventory system, feels like every day there’s some update to remember. I did help an older woman find the right size jacket and she was really grateful, which was nice.

It’s late and my legs still ache, but I keep thinking about whether I missed any bills. Phone bill’s due in a few days, so I set a reminder on my phone. After work I wanted to just crash, but ended up checking my budget again for the third time. I wish I could just relax and stop worrying, but I keep catching myself making lists in my head. Need to sleep, but I’m not really tired, just wired from the day. Maybe tomorrow I’ll actually go for a walk before work, clear my head a little.

The air was cool tonight as I walked around the block, my mind wandering even though my body felt so tired. I noticed the familiar porch lights flickering on as families settled in for the evening, and it made me think of how much has changed since Mom’s diagnosis. Work was non-stop today, a steady stream of clients with heavy stories, and I could feel my energy flagging by the time I got home. I tried to check in with my partner as soon as I walked through the door, but I think I came off distracted. Communication has been a project for us lately, and I keep reminding myself to be more present, but sometimes I just feel drained. During my walk, I called my brother to see how he was holding up with everything at home. He sounded tired too, but he was grateful that I asked. I wish I had more to give both at work and with my family, but tonight just feels like one of those nights when I’m running on fumes. I grabbed some groceries on the way back and thought about making soup, but ended up just microwaving leftovers. I’m hoping tomorrow I wake up with a little more energy to face the day, to be a better partner and daughter. For now, I’m just glad to have a quiet moment outside under the streetlights, listening to my own footsteps for a bit.

The lamp on this desk is too bright, but if I turn it off I can’t see the calendar or the pile of permission slips. It’s late and everyone else is asleep, but I still have two school forms to fill out, a dentist appointment to reschedule, and I’m not even sure if I signed up for the parent-teacher conference or just thought about it. I keep bumping into my wife in the hallway and we both look tired, barely talk except about drop-off times or who’s cooking. Feels like we’re business partners, not married people. Found a note from her about soccer practice in my jacket pocket, no time to talk in person. I keep forgetting to pack lunches the night before. The kids keep asking if we’re going to the park this weekend. I said yes but I haven’t checked our schedule and there’s that birthday party on Saturday. I barely get five minutes alone and even now, at this desk, I can hear someone’s shoes squeaking in the hallway. Every time I try to get ahead, something else lands on the list. I don’t know when this got so complicated or how to make it quieter.

The old desk chair creaks every time I shift, which is a lot. The afternoon sun is trying to get through the blinds, making weird patterns on the sketchbook I’m not using. I spent most of today jumping between emails, invoices, and a couple of client calls that all seemed to want something yesterday. It’s like every logistical thing that could pile up decided today was the day. I had this one call with a client who kept changing their mind about the color scheme, and I could feel my jaw clenching the longer it dragged on. At one point, I realized I hadn’t eaten since breakfast, but didn’t have it in me to do anything about it. There’s a half-finished painting staring at me from the shelf, and I keep thinking I should just drop everything and work on it instead of spreadsheets, but then the anxiety about rent sneaks in. I caught myself zoning out completely for a few minutes, staring at the wall and tuning out the sound of my phone buzzing again. There’s a kind of tiredness that comes from this constant switching between tasks, but my brain refuses to slow down. The only meaningful moment was when I finished one tiny sketch for myself, not for a client. It wasn’t much, but it felt like a small win in a day where I mostly felt like I was scrambling to keep up. Maybe tomorrow I’ll actually get to make something just because I want to.

Feeling a bit on edge this morning with the to-do list already circling my mind. I stood in the kitchen trying to focus on making oatmeal, but my mind kept drifting to the emails I need to answer from yesterday’s clients and the intake forms I haven’t set up for the new referral. I’m behind on sending invoices, which means payments will be even later this month. The unpredictability of freelancing is wearing on me, even though I keep telling myself it’s a trade-off for flexibility. I’m supposed to have a Zoom session at 8:30, but I still haven’t reviewed the client’s notes from last week. The fridge is emptier than I’d like, but I can’t justify stopping for groceries until I finish prepping for this morning’s sessions. I caught myself snapping at the kettle for boiling too slowly – not my finest moment. On top of that, the neighbor’s dog has been barking since 6, which hasn’t helped my nerves. I know I’ll settle into a rhythm once the day gets going, but right now it feels like everything is demanding attention at once. I need to remember to slow down, but it’s easier said than done.

The dishwasher made that weird clanking sound again after dinner and I told her we should really get it checked, but she just brushed it off, said it’s probably nothing. I know it’s not really about the dishwasher, though. We’ve both been tired lately, and even small things seem to turn into these mini standoffs. I tried to explain my point but somehow it ended up with her saying I never listen. That stung more than I expected, especially since I thought I was being patient. Maybe I’m missing something. It’s just hard to figure out what she needs sometimes, or if I’m just too focused on fixing things instead of hearing what she’s really saying. I keep replaying the conversation in my head, wondering if I should’ve just let it go. Everything feels heavier at night, especially when the house is quiet and there’s nothing left to distract me. I hope tomorrow feels lighter.

I just finished wiping crumbs from the counter for the third time tonight. Everyone else is asleep, the house is finally quiet, and I can hear the fridge humming behind me. I keep coming back to this kitchen like it’s the only place I can breathe, even if the air smells like last night’s soup.

Today was another round of dodging questions from my mother about how I’m “really doing.” She means well, but I’m so tired of talking circles around the obvious. Grief has taken up space here, even in the cabinets somehow. I noticed my son left his homework on the table, half-finished, and I thought about how much I wanted to just leave things half-done, too. But I picked it up and set it on his backpack anyway.

I barely wrote anything useful all day. The words just wouldn’t come, or if they did, they sounded hollow. I wonder if this is what it’s going to be like from now on. The restlessness isn’t helping. I tried making lists, thinking I could wrangle my brain into productivity, but mostly ended up doodling in the margins. Sometimes I think I’d get more done if I locked myself in the bathroom, though someone would bang on the door within five minutes.

Late nights like this, I start to overthink everything: my work, my health, how we’re all supposed to move forward without her. I keep telling myself that tomorrow will be easier, but I know that’s not guaranteed. For now, I’ll just listen to the fridge and hope the morning brings some clarity, or at least fewer crumbs.

I remember this morning standing in front of the fridge, staring at the shelves, trying to decide what I could put together for breakfast that wouldn’t mean another trip to the store this week. I kept thinking about the receipt I stuffed in my jacket pocket last night after buying groceries. The numbers keep running through my head, adding up slowly, as if each dollar spent is another ounce of pressure. I found myself counting eggs, thinking about how many slices of bread are left, and whether I could stretch the milk until Friday. It’s funny how all these little choices feel so heavy sometimes.

Now, sitting at the kitchen table with the dim light barely making the counters glow, I feel restless. My mind keeps bouncing between what needs to be done at work and what bills are due soon. I noticed the stack of unopened mail by the toaster, and I just felt tired looking at it. Honestly, it’s a mix of irritation and worry, because I know there’s a credit card statement in there I’ve been avoiding. Part of me wants to just get up and start sorting everything right now, but the other part wants to just sit and let the worry pass. I know I’m patient, but it’s wearing thin lately. I want to believe I can manage all this, but it feels like the logistics of life are just piling up and I’m so sensitive to every little glitch. This morning’s breakfast scramble wasn’t just about eating, it was about trying to keep control. Maybe later today, after work, I’ll feel a little more on top of things. For now I just wish the world would give me a break.

Birds are noisy tonight, all over the trees as I walk. Just did a lap around the block to clear my head after another impossible text exchange with M. We still can’t get on the same page about the weekends, even though I tried making a shared calendar and sent it twice. It’s like every appointment I mention turns into a negotiation. I stuck with practical questions but somehow things still veered off. I kept replaying what I said, trying to figure out if I was unclear or too blunt. I can’t afford to get distracted with deadlines coming up, but this stuff just follows me around. At least a walk helps me refocus, even if my phone keeps buzzing.

Muted car engines and the hum of tires on asphalt filter in through my window as I sit in the parking lot, trying to mentally line up the rest of my day. There’s a brightness to the afternoon that’s almost blinding, making me squint even though I’m still inside the car. I keep checking my phone to see if my roommate texted about whether she needs the car later, but so far, nothing. I’m already running through the list of forms I have to file at work, and there’s that meeting at three that always runs over. I forgot to pack lunch again, so maybe I’ll just grab something from the vending machine, if I remember before it’s too late and I end up with just a bag of pretzels. It’s my turn to pick up groceries tonight, but I’m not sure I’ll have time if traffic is bad, and my roommate needs the car back by seven for her class. I keep thinking I should start using one of those scheduling apps, but every time I download one, I get overwhelmed setting it up and give up halfway through.

There’s a pile of laundry at home that’s probably starting to smell, and I haven’t even thought about when I’ll get to that. I also promised my sister I’d call her this week, but I keep pushing it back because I can’t seem to find a free half hour where I’m not either at work or trying to get everything else done. I wish I could just press pause and sort out one thing at a time, but it feels like everything needs attention at once. The light in the parking lot is shifting now, shadows getting sharper. I should probably head in, but I want just a few more minutes to breathe before the next round of emails and requests starts piling up. Maybe if I can just get through today, tomorrow will be smoother, but that’s what I thought yesterday too.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
The hum of the fridge is louder than usual tonight, or maybe I’m just noticing it more. The living room is mostly dark except for the streetlight glow leaking in through the blinds. I’m looking at my planner again, trying to block off time for laundry, grocery shopping, and following up on emails I’ve put off for two days. There’s a pile of unopened mail on the coffee table and I can’t remember if I paid the water bill or just thought about paying it.

I keep thinking I should reach out to someone from work, maybe invite them for a walk, but I’m not sure if I’ll actually follow through. There are so many small things I haven’t finished, and they circle around in my head. I told myself I’d unpack the last moving box this weekend, but it’s still sitting by the door. I wonder if I’m making this harder than it needs to be, or if it just feels like a lot because everything is new. I’ll try to get some of it done tomorrow if I wake up early enough.

The hum of the fridge is the only thing breaking the quiet right now, and the glow from the TV screen makes everything look kind of blue. I haven’t bothered to turn on the main light because I like how the room gets softer at night. My mind keeps looping back to that weird conversation with my brother earlier. He called to check in, which was nice, but then we got on the topic of Dad and it got awkward fast. I don’t know if I misunderstood what he was asking or if he was fishing for something, but I felt like I was supposed to have some big insight about why Dad’s been distant lately. I just didn’t. Maybe he thinks I’m not paying attention, but honestly, I’m just tired of guessing what everyone wants from me.

I replayed the call after we hung up, trying to figure out if I’d sounded cold. I wanted to say, “I get how you feel,” but the words never came out right. Sometimes I wish I was better at these conversations, but I always end up hyperfocusing on little details, like the way he paused or changed the subject. Maybe I’m overcomplicating it. I know I care, but it’s easier to focus on work or my own routine than to dig into family stuff. Anyway, I’ll probably text him tomorrow, maybe ask if he wants to grab food this weekend. It feels like the right thing, even if I’m not sure what I want to say yet. For now, it’s just me, the fridge, and this weird blue light keeping me company.

The blue light from my laptop is the only thing lighting up the bedroom right now. I should probably close some of these tabs, but I keep thinking I’ll need them for tomorrow’s shipments. I spent most of the evening trying to coordinate between two teams who kept missing each other’s updates, and it feels like my brain’s stuck in logistics mode even though I’m supposed to be off the clock.

Had a short argument with Mia about dinner plans, which turned into a longer discussion about how I’m always distracted lately. I know she’s right. It’s not like I want to be glued to my screen, but every time I try to step away, there’s another Slack ping or some spreadsheet to double-check. Working from home sounded like a good idea last year, but now I barely know when work ends and the rest of life starts.

My mind keeps jumping between tomorrow’s delivery issues and whether I remembered to pay the utility bill. I’ve set up reminders for just about everything, but it still feels like things are slipping through the cracks. Maybe I’ll actually turn off my phone for an hour tomorrow and see if it helps. Right now, I just want a bit of quiet before the cycle starts all over again.

I feel jittery, kind of like I woke up halfway through a race I didn’t know I’d entered. The kitchen is too quiet except for the hum of the fridge, and I keep glancing at the clock, trying to figure out if I actually have time to get through my list today. There are boxes still stacked by the pantry that I haven’t touched since I moved in, but I keep putting off unpacking because there’s always something else that feels more urgent. My phone is already buzzing with reminders for job applications, follow-ups, and some interview I need to schedule for tomorrow. I keep making lists and rewriting them, but the tasks seem to multiply instead of shrinking. My brother texted about helping him move his couch this weekend, and I haven’t replied yet because I’m not sure I’ll be able to fit it in. Groceries are running low, and I keep forgetting to buy dish soap. I noticed the trash needs to go out, but I’m out of garbage bags. Every surface seems to have some half-finished project or paperwork on it. I’m trying to keep things orderly, but the more I try, the messier it feels. I know I’m supposed to be networking and reaching out to people, but I just don’t have the energy for small talk lately. Still, I’m glad I have that spreadsheet tracking my applications, because at least it feels like one thing is under control. Tonight I need to prep for that phone call with the recruiter, but I keep second-guessing what I should say. I wish I could just press pause for a day and get my bearings. Maybe I’ll make some tea and try to chip away at the boxes before it gets too late.

Feeling both energized and jittery this morning, probably because I woke up thinking about the call with my sister scheduled for this afternoon. It’s odd how even after all these years, our conversations can leave me a little uneasy. She texted last night reminding me about Mom’s birthday plans, but I’m honestly not sure I can commit to anything this week with my workload so scattered. There’s a stack of notes on the counter, and my laptop is already open, half a dozen tabs blinking at me with unfinished research requests. Freelancing keeps things interesting, but lining up enough projects to pay the bills is its own sort of background noise.

I keep replaying last month’s chat with her, when she seemed to think I was avoiding family stuff on purpose. That’s not it at all, but I haven’t figured out how to explain the unpredictability of my schedule without sounding like I’m making excuses. She’s always been more structured than me, which is probably why she gets frustrated. Maybe I’ll try to be more direct today, but I also don’t want the conversation to drift into old patterns. I’ll probably just make some tea and hope for the best. There’s only so much I can plan for, and at some point, I have to let the conversation go where it goes.

Just finished washing the last mug from yesterday, and it’s still too quiet in the kitchen. I kept thinking about that student who came up to me after class, asking for help with her essay. She looked so nervous, and I could tell she almost didn’t ask. I tried to give her some straightforward advice, but I’m not sure if I came off too blunt. I’m practical, not always gentle, and I wonder if that gets in the way sometimes. 

Late last night, after grading another stack of papers, I caught myself checking my bank app again. The numbers haven’t changed. It’s tiring, tracking every dollar, but I can’t let things slip. I keep telling myself I’m doing what I can, but it all feels scattered. Anyway, I hope I managed to help that student at least a little. That’s the part that should matter most.

The lamp on my desk is too bright tonight, making my eyes ache, but I can’t seem to get up and turn it off. All I can think about is the presentation I have to give tomorrow morning and how the mock-up just doesn’t feel right to me yet. I spent hours moving shapes around, changing fonts, tweaking the color palette, but nothing clicked. My mind keeps replaying the conversation with Mark from earlier, that tightness in his voice when he asked if I’d finished the revisions he wanted. I told him I’d get it done, but I could see he was annoyed, or maybe just stressed himself. It’s hard to tell sometimes, but I always end up worrying it’s my fault.

I tried to distract myself by texting Sarah, which ended up making things worse. She replied in short sentences, nothing like how we used to talk, and now I keep wondering if I said something wrong last week. I know I should let it go and just focus on my work, but everything feels tangled up together right now. The quiet in this apartment feels heavier than usual, maybe because I’m running on too little sleep. I keep thinking about how things used to be easier, or at least I didn’t notice the pressure as much. Maybe I’m just tired, or maybe I’m just not as good at handling this stuff as I thought. I wish I could shut my brain off for a bit, let the worries drift away, but lying in bed later I know I’ll just keep picking at all of this until I finally pass out.

I just turned off the ignition and sat here for a minute, trying to organize my thoughts before I head in. The parking lot is almost empty, which makes me feel both early and out of sync. There are lesson plans scattered on the passenger seat, and my laptop bag is digging into my side because I tossed it there in a hurry. I was reviewing emails right up until I parked, and I’m pretty sure I forgot to respond to one from the principal about next week’s schedule.

Remote work has blurred everything. I feel like my living room is still clinging to me, even as I try to mentally switch gears for in-person teaching today. I keep thinking about the stack of grading I left on my dining table, mixed in with grocery lists and half-finished coffee mugs. It’s hard to shake the feeling that I’m always halfway between two places, never fully present in either.

I can hear myself breathing a bit faster, probably because I’m running through today’s logistics in my head. Did I upload the handouts for my morning class? Did I print out the attendance sheets? These little details seem to multiply the more I try to get ahead. My phone buzzed twice while I was parking, but I ignored it because I just needed a second to pause.

I wish I was better at compartmentalizing. It seems like everything is bleeding together more and more lately, and I’m so restless I can barely focus. I wonder if other teachers feel like this, or if I’m just not adapting well. I’ll try to ground myself before I walk in, but right now it feels like I’m carrying all the unfinished tasks from home straight into work with me.

The hum of the fridge is louder than usual tonight, and the streetlights outside keep flickering through the curtains, making weird stripes on the wall. I’ve been stuck on the couch for the last hour, scrolling through my calendar app and trying to figure out how everyone’s schedules fit together for the week. It almost feels like a puzzle game that keeps changing the rules. My roommate came in earlier and asked if I’d remembered to switch my laundry. I had, but then he mentioned something about his girlfriend staying over on Friday and I realized I’d double-booked my own plans with some job applications I promised myself I’d finish. Now I’m not even sure if I should cancel or just try to hide out in my room all evening. 

It’s weird how much I care about these small overlaps and interruptions. I want to keep things smooth for everyone, but lately it’s like the more I plan, the more tangled it gets. Part of me wonders if I’m overthinking it and another part is worried that if I don’t stay on top of every little thing, I’ll mess up and people will get annoyed. My roommate didn’t seem mad, but sometimes I can’t tell. I probably should have just asked him directly if it was okay for me to be around or if they needed space. Instead, I just nodded and tried to act casual. I know I’m unemployed right now and maybe I’m being too sensitive about taking up space or not pulling my weight, but I really do want things to work out. I keep thinking if I get my next steps right, things will settle down, but there’s always another snag. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try talking to him again, even if it feels awkward. For now, I just keep rearranging my plans and hoping I’m not making things harder for everyone.

Just closed my laptop and sat back on the couch, trying to get my breathing under control. It’s been nonstop today, shuttling between work emails, spreadsheets, and the group chat with Alex about the kids’ schedule. We had another argument over who’s picking up from soccer practice Friday. I tried so hard to keep it calm, but I could feel my voice getting tight, and I hate that. He’s so quick to get defensive, and I know I can be controlling about the schedule, but someone has to be or nothing gets done.

At the same time, my boss messaged asking for the monthly report a day early, so I’ve been jumping between tabs and my phone all afternoon. I keep thinking it’s all going to fall apart, but it never does, somehow. Maybe I need to let go a little. I did text Alex an apology for snapping at him, and he wrote back, "It’s okay, we’re both tired." That helped, but I’m still wound up. I keep telling myself things will get easier with time. For now, I’m just trying to remember to breathe and get through one thing at a time.

Steam from the kettle fogged up my glasses as I waited for it to boil. The kitchen is chilly this morning, even though it’s technically summer. I keep glancing at the calendar on the fridge, thinking about all the bills coming up this week.

Yesterday was tense with Marcia at work. She snapped when I asked about the new schedule, and I know I probably sounded nervous. I hate feeling like I’m bothering people, but I never seem to say things the right way. Sometimes I wish I could just blend into the background at the office, do my work, and not have to worry about anyone’s mood but my own.

My hands shake a little pouring tea. I keep running through yesterday’s conversation in my head, wondering if I should apologize or just let it go. I wish I could stop replaying things and just focus on the day. There’s too much to keep track of, money-wise and otherwise. Maybe things will feel better after I get through this week. For now, I just need to get through the morning.

Finished clearing the dishes after dinner and sat down to try to make sense of the day. I packed boxes at the warehouse again, and the pace was relentless. Since we moved, I keep feeling like I’m one step behind, both at home and at work. The new shift manager keeps changing the way we organize shipments, so nothing feels settled. I spent half the morning searching for misplaced inventory, which put me behind on my own tasks. Even after years in this job, I still get irritated when things seem unnecessarily complicated. The noise in the warehouse gets to me sometimes, especially when I’m already feeling restless. I tried talking to a couple of the guys during break, but everyone seemed preoccupied or tired, so the conversation didn’t go far. Coming home is a relief, even if the house still doesn’t feel like ours yet. There are boxes in the hallway and the living room, and I keep forgetting where we put basic stuff like the can opener. I know it’ll get better, but tonight I just feel a bit scattered. Going to try to read for a bit before bed, though I doubt I’ll make it through more than a few pages. Maybe tomorrow I’ll make a list and try to tackle things one at a time.

This afternoon, I was worrying about a late payment from a client as I took a walk around the block to clear my head. I kept checking my phone, half hoping for an email, half knowing it wouldn’t come that quickly. The uncertainty of freelancing gets under my skin sometimes, even though I tell myself it’s part of the deal. While I walked, I noticed the way the sunlight bounced off the neighbor’s windows and the smell of someone grilling nearby. It reminded me that there’s a bigger world outside my inbox, and I felt my shoulders loosen up a bit. I let myself imagine a future with steadier work, but then caught myself and tried to just focus on the present moment. It’s hard to stay optimistic, but I’m proud that I still am, most days. Even being able to take this walk in the middle of the day is a kind of freedom. I know I’ll figure things out, even if the waiting feels endless sometimes.
