I also need to follow up on that email from last week and update my resume with those new skills I learned, but the to-do list keeps growing faster than I can keep up. On top of that, I remembered earlier that we have to finalize plans for the weekend with his family, and I’m not even sure what we’re supposed to bring. Communication with him has been better lately, at least, but there are still moments when I can tell we’re both tired and trying not to snap at each other. I wanted to talk more about how we’re dividing up chores, but we ended up just watching TV in silence instead. It’s hard to bring up little frustrations when I already feel like I’m barely keeping my own head above water. Earlier tonight I skipped dinner because I was so caught up in tasks, and now my stomach is grumbling. There’s laundry waiting in the basket, dishes in the sink, and the bathroom really needs to be cleaned but I can’t find the motivation. I keep thinking if I just get more organized, I’ll finally feel on top of things, but every day something new pops up. I wish I could turn off my brain for a bit or at least feel like I’m making real progress somewhere. Maybe tomorrow I’ll manage to cross a few things off the list, but right now it just feels endless.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
This morning I was sitting in the hallway before class started, waiting for the professor to unlock the door, and I overheard two of my classmates talking about the job fair next week. I got the courage to ask them if they felt ready, and one of them just shrugged and said, "I guess?" but the other seemed so confident, listing off all the companies she wanted to talk to. I nodded along and tried to sound like I have a plan, but inside I felt like I was faking it. Now, during my lunch break, it's quiet enough that I can actually hear myself think, which is both a blessing and a curse. My mind keeps circling back to that conversation, wishing I could just ask them how they manage all this uncertainty. Are they actually confident, or just pretending? Maybe everyone is pretending at least a little.

I feel scattered, like I should be using this time to prepare for interviews or at least look through job listings, but my brain just wants to rest. It's hard to juggle class assignments, job applications, and trying to figure out who I am in the middle of all this. Am I a student, or a job seeker, or both, or neither yet? I wish there was someone I could be completely honest with about how lost I feel, but even when I try to talk to my family, I end up minimizing everything because I don't want to worry them. I keep telling myself to be patient, that things will work out, but some days it's tough to believe it. For now, I'll just finish my sandwich and try not to overthink what comes next.

This morning I remembered standing in the kitchen, halfway through making toast, when I realized the milk was expired and the recycling still hadn’t gone out. I left both half-finished, thinking I’d circle back, but I didn’t. Now I’m circling the block, walking fast, almost like I’m trying to catch up with all the stuff I’ve let dangle throughout the day. The list of things I need to do is ridiculous: send the edits back to Dr. F, invoice for the last dataset, figure out if I can afford groceries before Friday, and double-check if I missed a meeting invite buried somewhere in my inbox. The phone keeps buzzing, mostly with reminders I set for myself, which is both helpful and completely annoying. 

I’m trying to keep organized, but it’s like every time I finish one task, two more appear. I had a brief moment of clarity about what I actually want from this freelance patchwork, but it vanished as soon as I started thinking about rent and deadlines. I keep thinking I should make a master list, but then I get distracted by the next thing that pops up, so the list is just scattered notes on my phone and scraps of paper in my bag. My head is full of project outlines and half-finished grocery lists. Walking helps, a little. I can’t really tell if I’m moving toward anything or just staying busy, but at least I’m moving. Maybe tonight I’ll actually finish something. Or at least remember to buy more milk.

Walked around the block tonight after dinner, it was already dark but the air felt good, cool on my arms. Streetlights flickering, a couple cars driving by, nobody else really out except that guy with the big dog. I kept thinking about how I spend so much time just going through the same routines, work then home, TV, bed. Sometimes I wonder if this is it, you know? Like, am I missing something or is this just what life is for someone like me? Had a weird moment where I stared into a window, saw my reflection, and it looked like a stranger for a second. My mind was racing about work stuff, emails I forgot, did I shut down my computer right, and then suddenly I’m thinking about where I’ll be in five years. It’s all jumbled together, hard to untangle. I like the quiet and the predictability, but then I get restless, anxious that I’m not doing enough, or being enough. I caught myself counting steps, not because I care about fitness but just to have something to focus on. The smell of someone’s laundry vent hit me, reminded me I need to do mine, and then I was thinking about how much I hate folding shirts. I guess I feel like I should want more, or at least know what I want, but I don’t. Patient with myself, trying not to judge, but also kind of frustrated. Sometimes I wish something would happen, just to shake things up, but I also know I’d probably panic if it did. Wrapped up the walk by checking my phone for no reason, nothing new. I’ll probably snack and watch that documentary before bed, and tomorrow’ll look a lot like today.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
I got home about an hour ago and realized I forgot to grade those last five assignments sitting in my bag. I meant to do them right after dinner, but honestly, my brain just feels like mush right now. It was a regular day at school but somehow more tiring than usual, maybe because I had to cover for another teacher last-minute and that threw off my whole routine. I was short with a couple of students during group work, and I noticed, but I just didn’t have the energy to fake patience. I keep thinking I should be handling the workload better by now. I’ve been a teacher for a few years and I’m still juggling finishing my own classes, but sometimes it feels like I’m never making real progress, just staying afloat.

I sat on the couch for half an hour after getting home, just scrolling on my phone and not really seeing anything. I tried to read over my notes for my own online class that’s due tomorrow but the words kept blurring together. I know I should just go to bed and try again in the morning. It’s late and I can hear the fridge humming in the quiet, but I keep replaying some stupid conversation I had in the break room about why I’m still taking classes when I’m already teaching. I didn’t really have an answer. Maybe I’m just hoping for something to click, or for things to feel less up in the air. I guess that’s enough for tonight. I’ll try to get up early and see if my head’s clearer.

I spent most of this morning double-checking some code I wrote yesterday, but my mind kept drifting back to the call I had with Mom before work. She sounded tired, and her voice was quieter than usual, which has been happening more often since Dad passed. I tried to ask about her doctor’s appointment without making her feel like I was prying. She said everything is "routine" but I could hear something else underneath, maybe just sadness, maybe more. It's hard to focus on technical details when the bigger questions about her health and how she's really coping keep sneaking in.

During my lunch break, I sat quietly at my kitchen table and replayed parts of our conversation. The fog in my head hasn't really lifted, and I keep wondering if I should visit soon, even though I know she always says she doesn’t want me to worry or rearrange my life. I wish I could do more than just call. I feel anxious but also hopeful that with time, both of us will find a new kind of normal. For now, I’ll keep checking in, even if it’s just to hear her talk about the weather or what she’s cooking for dinner.

My hands are cold from gripping the steering wheel, even though the car’s heater has been running for a while. I’m parked in my usual spot, a little farther from the school entrance than I’d like, but early enough that it’s quiet except for the sound of a few other cars pulling in. I can already feel the tension in my shoulders from thinking about another day of managing the classroom. Some days I wish I could sit here a little longer and just let the world go on without me for a bit.

This morning, I argued with my sister over the bathroom again. She always takes forever, and with everyone rushing around the house, it’s impossible to get a moment alone. I know it’s petty, but it left me irritable. I keep replaying what I said to her, wishing I’d just kept my mouth shut. I love my family, but sometimes I wonder what it would be like to have a space of my own where I could just breathe. Now I need to switch gears and put on my patient teacher face. The kids will be loud, some will test my patience, and the day will feel long, but maybe I’ll find a small moment of calm in the chaos. For now, I just need to gather myself before stepping out into the noise. I’m tired, but hopefully I’ll find some energy as the day goes on.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
Just finished double-checking tomorrow’s reading assignments while the bus rattled past the downtown lights. The city still feels unfamiliar, especially at night, and I keep reminding myself not to miss my stop. My mind is jumping between the group project meeting earlier (awkward as usual) and everything I still need to get done before the weekend. I tried to contribute more today, but I always wonder if I come across as too blunt or just out of sync with everyone else. Maybe I shouldn’t have corrected Mark about the due date, but I couldn’t help it. 

There’s also the issue of my schedule for next week. I have a paper due Monday, plus the online quiz that I almost forgot about. I have to email the librarian about getting access to those articles, and I still need to figure out groceries since I’m almost out of coffee and cereal. I keep making lists, but it feels like I’m always adding more than I cross off. No one here really knows me yet, which is both a relief and a weight. I hope I can find a better rhythm soon, but tonight it’s just me, my planner, and this restless energy.

This morning at the shop, I accidentally grabbed the wrong socket for the third time in a row. I had to laugh it off, but I could tell my head wasn’t really in it. I was thinking about the late job from yesterday and all the stuff I’ve still got to organize at home. It’s like my brain is juggling wrenches and schedules at the same time, and both keep slipping. Managed to patch up that old Civic, but I kept checking my phone to remind myself about rent, setting up utilities, and trying to remember where I put the box with my extra work gloves.

Now I’m sitting at my desk, staring at a pile of unopened mail and the notepad where I tried to make a list of things I need to do. I keep starting lists but then losing them or forgetting what’s on them. I know I should set up my bank account here and call my sister back, but the thought of it just makes me tired. There’s still unpacked boxes in the corner, and the only thing I’ve managed to really set up is my alarm clock. I keep telling myself I’ll get a handle on all this, but tonight it feels like I’m just barely keeping up with the basics.

The sunlight today is sharp through the blinds, landing in stripes across my keyboard. It’s almost too bright to look at the screen, but I can’t move because my schedule feels packed and I need every minute. Meetings seemed to stack one on top of another, and I kept waiting for a break that didn’t come. Slack notifications kept buzzing, a reminder of all the small things I still owe people. I tried to answer everyone, but it felt like I was falling behind anyway.

A disagreement with one of the team leads lingered in my mind longer than I expected. We didn’t see eye to eye on priorities for this week, and I could feel the tension even though we were both trying to keep the conversation polite. I wish I could smooth it over quickly, but I also know we both care a lot. It’s hard to stay warm and gentle when I’m tired and juggling so many things. My optimism helps, but right now I just want an hour with no messages, no calls, and no decisions to make. Maybe I’ll step outside for a walk before the next call.

The car heater is humming while I sit here in the parking lot, headlights of other cars flickering past. I’m still thinking about last night, how loud it got in the kitchen even though everyone was trying to talk quietly. Kids were pretending not to listen but I know they caught parts of it. I should’ve just dropped the whole thing when she said she was tired, but instead I had to bring up the bills and the missing receipts. Didn’t even remember where I put half of them myself.

Now it’s early, I barely slept, and I can’t shake the feeling that everything’s hanging in the air, unfinished. I keep replaying how she walked off to fold laundry instead of answering me. The cupboards are still open, cereal boxes out, and I left my work papers on the table. I need to apologize, I guess, but don’t know if I have the energy to sort through it all tonight. Got to get my head together before I go in, but my mind keeps drifting to home. Maybe pick up something for dinner on the way back, try to make it a quieter night. Just want things to settle down for a bit.

Feeling a bit frazzled this morning, honestly. The bus ride home is the first time today I've actually had a chance to just sit, which is funny since the day barely started and I already feel like I ran a marathon. There were so many moving pieces to juggle earlier: the supplier was late with the shipment update, and then the payroll system decided to glitch out right as I was about to send salaries. I ended up with four different tabs open, two spreadsheets, and my phone ringing in the background while I tried to make sense of it all. Sometimes I wonder if I'm really cut out for this founder life or if I’m just riding the chaos hoping it’ll settle down by itself. The remote work thing doesn’t help. Home blends into work so much that I catch myself thinking about delivery schedules while making toast, then forgetting what I was doing in the first place.

Still, I managed to sort out the payroll mess before noon, so that’s a small win. I even remembered to reply to that investor email, though my answer was probably longer than it needed to be (classic me). On the bus now, I keep thinking about whether I should set harder stop times, or just accept that this is how things are in my world for now. I do like the flexibility, but wow, the logistics stack up fast and sometimes my mind gets tangled in all the details. I guess I’m optimistic that it’ll get easier as things grow, or maybe I’ll just get better at letting the small stuff roll off. I need to remember to breathe, take it one thing at a time, and maybe actually look out the window instead of at my phone for once. 🚌

My sandwich is getting cold because I keep replaying this morning in my head. When I dropped off Ava at her dad’s, he barely looked at me and just said, "You’re late again." I was only six minutes late, but it’s always something. I tried to explain that traffic was awful and Ava needed her jacket, but he just shut the door. I stood there for a second, holding her backpack, and just felt so small. Every time we have to coordinate these drop-offs, I brace myself for another little jab. I know I’m organized, I have every calendar invite and reminder set, but it never feels good enough. It’s exhausting trying to keep everything straight and still get judged. Sometimes I wonder if it would just be easier to stop caring, but then I think about Ava and I can’t. I wish he’d just meet me halfway on this instead of making it into a contest. My break is almost over and I’m still stuck in that moment, wishing things could be less tense.

The sunlight is coming through the break room window and it’s kind of nice to have some quiet for once. I brought my lunch from home again because I can’t really justify spending anything extra right now. I kept looking at job listings on my phone but it’s all starting to blur together. Sometimes I wonder if I’m even applying for the right things or just anything that looks halfway doable. It’s weird not having a routine and not really knowing what comes next, but at least I’m keeping a close eye on all my expenses so I don’t get caught off guard. My mind keeps drifting to what I actually want to do long term, and then I get distracted by a notification or a random thought. I guess for now I just need to focus on getting something stable, even if it’s not perfect. Maybe I’ll try to organize my job search later today, but for now I just want to eat in peace.

The hum of the fridge is louder this morning, probably because the house is actually quiet for once. Pale light from the window is just starting to hit the tile, which means I have about ten minutes before someone else comes in looking for breakfast or starts asking where their socks are. I’m already thinking about the list for today: Dad’s medication at eight, Mom’s doctor call at nine, laundry that’s piling up in the hallway, and trying to remember who needs to be where and when. I scribbled a schedule on the notepad last night but can’t even find it now, which is typical. 

My head is tired before the day really starts. I keep wondering if I’m actually doing a good job or if I’m just barely managing to keep everyone from falling apart. There’s never a finished feeling, just one thing after another. I miss having a door I could close for even half an hour. The kitchen is the only spot I can claim for a few minutes, but even here, I hear footsteps upstairs and know it’s almost over. I wish I could find a way to feel less scattered or stop worrying that I’m forgetting something crucial. Maybe when everyone leaves for school and work, I’ll actually sit with a cup of tea, but I doubt it.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text:
Tired but couldn’t sleep, ended up at the desk with stacks of papers and my laptop open, emails piling up. Not sure if it was work or the thought of Anna that kept my brain spinning. The past few days have been a mess: two investor calls (one ran over, had to reschedule with the team), product roadmap keeps shifting, and now there’s a bug in the last release. I feel like I’m always on the edge of dropping something important. Phone kept buzzing with Slack notifications until I finally muted it, but even then it felt like there was more I should be doing.

Anna texted around midnight, just a simple "hey, hope you’re okay," but it threw me. We haven’t really figured out what this is, and I keep second-guessing every move. Work is bleeding into everything. I wanted to call her back but ended up just scrolling through old messages instead. The desk lamp was too bright, so I turned it off and sat in the dark for a bit, hoping it would help me focus. Ended up just making a list for tomorrow, nothing fancy, but at least now I won’t forget the morning call. Still feels like I’m barely keeping up with any of it.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text: Tonight on the bus ride home, my mind keeps going back to the phone call with Mom earlier. She asked how things were in the new city and I could hear the worry in her voice, that little hesitation after each question like she’s not sure how much to ask. I tried to sound upbeat, told her about the weird street performer I saw near the station, but she circled back to Dad’s anniversary coming up. I know she wants to talk about him, but I never know if I’m supposed to keep things light or let the conversation get heavy. I told her I’d light a candle, which is true, but I could tell she was hoping for something more, maybe a memory or just to hear his name. Part of me wanted to share how lonely I get here sometimes, especially around dates like this, but I held back because I didn’t want her to worry even more. There’s this strange balance between being honest and protecting her feelings, and I never feel like I get it quite right. The city lights outside the bus window look so different from home, and sometimes I wonder if I’ll ever really settle in here or if it’s always going to feel like I’m visiting. Maybe I should have just said that to her. Or maybe that would have made it harder for both of us. I wish I knew how to talk to her about missing Dad without making her sadder. All these years and I still stumble over the same things.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text:
The hum of the heater fills this room tonight, with just enough light from the desk lamp to make things feel cozy but not bright. I can hear the distant TV in the living room, but it’s muffled, almost like background noise in a dream. Sitting here at my desk, I keep thinking about the conversation I had today at work with Lorraine. She cornered me after lunch, asking if I’d finished the new care plan forms, and I felt that old pressure building in my chest.

Normally I don’t mind people checking in, but she had this edge to her voice, impatient, maybe even frustrated. I tried to answer as calmly as possible, told her I was working through them and had a few left, but she frowned and said something about timelines slipping. I wanted to remind her that I was covering shifts for two people today, but the words stuck. Instead, I just nodded and promised I’d get them done by the end of my shift.

Walking back to my desk, I couldn’t help but wonder if I’m really keeping up or just barely scraping by. The paperwork never ends, and it feels like I’m always one step behind. I wish I could explain to Lorraine that sometimes just getting through the day is enough, especially when there’s so much else on my mind. With the new relationship, I’m tired all the time, but I’m also hopeful, even if I don’t know what’s coming next.

Maybe Lorraine is under pressure herself, and I’m just an easy target. I don’t want to overthink it, but sometimes these little moments stick with me longer than I expect. I keep telling myself tomorrow is a new day, and maybe things will feel less heavy. For now, the heater hums, and I’ll try to let it all fade into the background so I can get some sleep.

My legs are propped up on the coffee table, and the sun is hitting the far wall just right, making the dust motes look like confetti. I woke up earlier than I meant to because my phone wouldn’t stop buzzing with notifications from a client who apparently doesn’t believe in time zones. I tried to ignore it, but then I started thinking about my invoice from last week that still hasn’t been paid. It’s always a toss-up whether these folks will pay on time, and I get way too anxious about it. I know that’s just how freelancing is, but it still gets under my skin.

Despite that, I managed to answer three tickets before 9 AM, which feels like a small win. The cat jumped up and demanded attention during my video call, which could have been embarrassing, but the client laughed it off. I’ve got two more support sessions scheduled for later, and I need to prep. I keep telling myself I’ll get better at balancing this, but I still struggle with boundaries. If I’m honest, I’m tired, but I’m also glad there’s work to do. The living room is cluttered, but that’s a problem for later. For now, I’m just trying to keep my mind on one thing at a time, which, given how scattered I feel, is almost impressive.

Just closed my laptop after another long shift and sat here at my desk, mostly just staring at the wall for a few minutes. I texted Jenna, finally, after avoiding it all day, and I’m still not sure if that was the right move. The argument we had last night keeps playing in my head, especially the part where she said I never really listen because I’m always half-distracted by work. She’s not totally wrong, but it stings to hear it spelled out like that. I keep telling myself I’m doing my best, but with work seeping into every corner of home, it’s like there’s no real break. Sometimes I wonder if I’m just using work as an excuse to avoid the tough conversations. The apartment feels quieter than usual, probably because I haven’t had music on or anything, just trying to focus and clear my head. I sent her a long message, trying to explain how I’m feeling and saying I want to fix things, but now I’m second-guessing every word. I want things to go back to normal, whatever that means, but I honestly don’t know what normal is supposed to look like anymore. Part of me wants to call her and just talk, but I’m afraid it’ll make things worse if I push too hard. I guess I’m just restless, sitting here waiting for her reply and trying not to check my phone every five seconds. I wish I could just compartmentalize everything neatly like I do with my emails and tasks, but feelings don’t work that way.

Trying to remember if I put the right forms in the trunk or if I left them by the laundry again. That’s how last night started: shuffling around the kitchen with everyone asking about their own stuff, and then my partner asked if I’d remembered to RSVP for my aunt’s birthday. I said yes, but I hadn’t, and then got caught in a pointless loop about why I always forget "small" things and whether they’re actually small. Sometimes I wonder if I should just own up to being the unreliable one, but that feels dramatic and probably isn’t true.

We ended up bickering, in front of the kids, which I hate. It wasn’t even about the RSVP, really, more like the slow drip of little missed details. My oldest tried to make a joke to cut the tension, which almost worked, but then my partner got quiet and started checking their phone. I wanted to say something light, but everything sounded sarcastic in my head, so I just loaded the dishwasher louder than necessary.

Now, parked here, I keep replaying the conversation and wondering if we’re both overcomplicating things. Or maybe I just am. Not sure if I should text an apology or just let the day play out. Feels like I’m always carrying some unfinished conversation into the next morning. Anyway, I need to double-check for those forms before I go in.

Just sent out another round of job applications while waiting for the bus, which felt like both a relief and a waste of time at the same time. I keep rereading my cover letters and thinking they sound too desperate, but then again, not sending anything would be even worse. The bus ride home is long enough to get lost in my head, and tonight I kept flipping between checking my messages from my kid’s mom about switching weekends and scrolling job boards. It’s like my brain can’t focus on anything for more than a couple minutes. I wanted to text her back with a clear answer, but then I remembered I need to double-check my own schedule, and now I’m worried I already committed to something else next Saturday.

I probably should have been more organized about my week, especially since interviews might actually get scheduled soon. I keep telling myself I’ll set a reminder or use a calendar app, but I always forget or get distracted. There’s a weird mix of hope and frustration, like maybe something will finally work out, but also expecting to screw it up somehow. Sometimes I wonder if other people my age feel this scattered or if I’m just missing some basic adulting skill. Anyway, by the time the bus pulled up to my stop I still hadn’t answered half my texts. I’ll deal with it in the morning, I guess. For now, I just want to zone out and not think about anything for a while.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
Just finished cramming for my quiz while sitting on this worn-out couch, tools still in my backpack from last night’s late shift. I barely had time to eat breakfast, let alone actually study the way I wanted, but I did what I could. My hands still smell faintly like grease and it’s weird trying to focus on textbooks when my brain is half stuck on a stubborn engine I didn’t finish fixing. Had this moment where I stopped and realized I’m actually making it work, even if it all feels like a scramble. That felt good, even if it only lasted a few seconds before the next thing popped up.

I know I complain about being tired and stretched thin, but there’s something kind of satisfying about it too. I’m not drifting, even though I feel restless all the time. I’m actually going somewhere, even if it’s not clear exactly where yet. Maybe that’s what hope feels like. Anyway, I have to get moving or I’ll be late for class. Not exactly the peace I want, but it’s enough for now.

My pen keeps rolling off the desk and it’s irritating. I didn’t sleep well last night, kept waking up thinking about Mom. This morning I found myself staring at my phone for fifteen minutes before I even got out of bed. It’s too quiet here, even with the window open and street noise drifting in.

Work is work. The new hospital feels different, the routines are all slightly off from what I’m used to, so I keep second-guessing myself. I had to double-check charting twice today. There was a patient who reminded me of Dad, which made me feel weirdly emotional in the middle of a dressing change. I didn’t say anything, just finished up and took a longer break in the stairwell. I texted my sister about it, but she just sent a thumbs-up emoji.

I still haven’t unpacked everything. I opened a box looking for my stethoscope and found old family photos instead. Couldn’t look at them for more than a minute. I keep telling myself it’ll get easier to feel settled, but right now it’s like I’m floating. Might go for a run later if the rain stops. Or maybe just order takeout and try to get my head together before another shift tomorrow.

My head feels weirdly cloudy today, and I’m not sure if it’s the weather or just me overthinking last night’s argument. I’m parked outside the client’s office, engine still running, replaying that conversation with Sam about weekend plans. We were both tired and it turned into this pointless back-and-forth about who initiates things more, which sounds dumb now but felt huge in the moment. I tried to joke my way out of it, but that only made things worse, like I was minimizing what Sam was trying to say.

Now I’m just sitting here, not really sure what the right next move is. Part of me wants to text something light and pretend nothing happened, but I know that’s the old pattern we’re supposed to be breaking. Sam actually brought up how I tend to dodge real talks with bad humor, and it stung because it’s true. I want to believe we’re getting better at this, but honestly, it all feels stuck and I can’t tell if it’s me, us, or just one of those dumb cycles couples go through.

I guess I’ll try to focus on work for a few hours and not spiral. Maybe by tonight the fog in my head will clear a bit, and I’ll figure out what to say. Or maybe I’ll just pick up dinner and hope that’s enough of a start. We’ll see.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
Feeling a bit overwhelmed this afternoon. The bus is packed, and my head is spinning with all the family logistics I need to sort out before the week is up. I keep running through the list: pick up prescriptions for Mom, call the plumber about the leak at Dad's place, and somehow squeeze in time to help Maya with her science project before Friday.

I still have a group assignment due for class, and work wants me to check in on the server migration tonight. Every time I think I’ve finished something, another thing pops up. My phone buzzed three times just now with reminders, and I can’t even remember if I replied to my sister’s text about dinner on Sunday.

I’m trying to stay focused and not let the anxiety get to me, but it feels like I’m just moving things around instead of actually getting them done. Maybe if I write it all out again when I get home, I’ll see a better way to juggle it. For now, I just need to remember to breathe and not miss my stop.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text:
Had to reschedule the investor call again, which meant pushing my morning workout to the imaginary slot called “later.” I was on the couch trying to reply to emails before he woke up. He wandered in, looking for his missing charger, and I realized I hadn’t figured out what to say about last night’s weird conversation.

I’m juggling onboarding for the new hire, the legal doc review, and now this relationship that seems to require as many calendar invites as my business. He made coffee, said something about us taking a weekend trip, and I mumbled an answer before remembering I had back-to-back calls all Saturday. Maybe I should have said yes. Or just anything that sounded committed.

The living room is cluttered with his stuff and my laptop cords. I keep thinking I’ll find time to tidy up and actually talk to him properly, but the day keeps filling up faster than I can cross things off. I don’t know how other people make space for this. Probably they don’t schedule love between Zoom meetings.

Had to restock the greeting cards this afternoon, which sounds simple but those racks are always a disaster. I wasted a good part of my lunch break digging through piles of "Happy Birthday" and "Get Well Soon" cards that looked like they’d survived a tornado. My sandwich kept getting squished in my bag, so I ended up eating half-mashed turkey and lettuce while crouched behind the loading door, trying not to get mustard on my shirt. The radio in the staff room was playing some upbeat pop song, which felt oddly out of place with how tired everyone looked. 

Even though it’s busy today, I feel a little lighter than usual. Maybe it’s just having a routine that helps. I caught myself making dumb jokes with the other associates while we organized the clearance shelf. No one really laughed, but at least no one looked annoyed either, which I’ll count as a win. My manager asked me to cover a shift tomorrow, and I said yes without really thinking it through. I guess I don’t mind the extra hours, but my head feels all over the place lately. Still, it’s nice to have things to do. After work I’ll probably just microwave some leftovers and watch something mindless before bed. Living alone has its perks, like not having to share the remote, but it also means I’m the only one who cleans up the mess. Not that I’ve been keeping up with that very well lately. I’ll try to get to the dishes tomorrow if I remember.

I feel scattered today, more than usual. Sitting at my desk with the door half-closed, I keep hearing everyone in the hallway and it’s hard to focus on what I need to do. There’s a list of job applications on my laptop, but every time I start one, someone calls me from the kitchen or asks if I’ve taken care of something for mom. I told myself I’d finish at least three applications before lunch, but it’s late afternoon and I’ve barely managed one.

My brother needed help with his paperwork, and then there was a phone call about dad’s next doctor’s appointment. I know these things are important, but I wish I could just close the door fully and have a few uninterrupted hours. My mind keeps jumping between helping out, worrying about my own future, and feeling guilty for not doing enough on either side. I keep adding reminders to my phone, but the list just gets longer. Maybe if I wake up earlier tomorrow, I can get a head start. For now, I just feel tired and behind on everything.

This morning, I remembered how we snapped at each other over Zoom last night. It was over something stupid, like who forgot to mute during my seminar. Woke up still feeling tense, even though I pretended everything was fine. Spent most of the day at my desk, bedroom door shut, trying to get through readings but checking my phone every ten minutes. He sent a couple of short texts, just about dinner and a meme, nothing about what happened. I didn’t reply right away. It’s weird because we’re in the same apartment but just messaging instead of talking. Remote work blurs everything, even the fights. I kept replaying how I sounded, if I was too sharp, if he’s annoyed. Tried to focus on data analysis, but my mind kept drifting. When he walked by to get coffee, we didn’t make eye contact. I wanted to say something, maybe just ask how his meeting went, but I stayed quiet. Tonight I know we’ll have to talk, but it feels easier to just stay here at my desk, headphones in, acting busy. I’m tired of the silence, but not sure how to break it yet.

Earlier this afternoon, I was standing in the hallway, calendar in hand, trying to figure out which parent pickup was mine and which was Jamie’s. I remember looking at all the sticky notes on the fridge (yellow ones are mine, blue ones are Jamie’s, the kids have their own colors too) and just feeling this weird sense of calm even though everything looked like chaos. I sat down at my bedroom desk to try to sort out the mess, laptop open to three tabs: school portal, work email, and a grocery list. The funny part is, I actually felt okay about it all. Maybe I’ve gotten used to the juggling. There was a moment when the phone rang and it was my son, asking if I could come to his rehearsal instead of Jamie, and I just wanted to say yes right away. But I had a meeting I couldn’t move, and he sounded disappointed but tried to hide it. That moment stuck with me for the rest of the day, just echoing in the background as I sent emails and booked appointments. I think what hit me was how much I want to be everywhere for everyone, but the logistics just won’t let me. Even coordinating with Jamie feels like running a small company sometimes. We managed, though. Later, when I checked the calendar one more time before dinner, everything was in its place. It’s not perfect, but it works most of the time. Sitting here now, the house is finally quiet, and I’m realizing that even though my days are packed and sometimes feel out of control, it’s the small moments like that phone call that make me stop and feel something real. I guess I’m grateful I noticed it instead of just pushing through. Maybe that’s the optimistic part of me. Tomorrow is another day of schedules and reminders, but for now, I’m just letting the quiet settle in.

Earlier this afternoon, I called Dad between projects and we talked for a while. He sounded distracted, as if he was thinking about something else the whole time, and I found myself getting frustrated when he didn’t really answer my questions about how he’s been feeling lately. I asked if he’d taken his medication, and he just said yes without any elaboration. I know I can be persistent but it’s hard not to repeat myself when I don’t feel like I’m actually getting through. Now, sitting on this crowded bus with the city lights blurring past, I keep replaying the conversation. Maybe I pushed too hard or maybe he just didn’t want to talk. It’s hard to know when to back off and when to press for details, especially with everything that’s happened this year. Working from home means I have all this flexibility, but it also means I can’t turn off the part of my brain that worries about him. I wish I could just drop by his place and see for myself, but it’s late and I’m tired. I guess I’ll try again tomorrow, or maybe I’ll just send a text and hope for a reply.

The dryer just finished its cycle and the sound startled me, even though I was expecting it. It’s almost midnight and I’m only now folding laundry, trying to clear my head after a long day of clients. Communication was a big topic today, both at work and at home. My partner and I had another tense conversation about splitting up chores and scheduling time together. It’s starting to feel like every logistical detail becomes a negotiation. I found myself getting impatient (internally, at least) even though I know I’m supposed to model calm and patience. Hard to practice what I preach when I’m tired. We have a shared calendar but it’s always getting out of date, and I’m not sure if it’s helping or making things worse. I suggested we try sitting down once a week to go over our plans, but even that turned into a debate about when we’re both free. I’m noticing that after a full day of listening to other people, I have very little left over for my own relationship. It feels like my brain is constantly managing lists: client notes, session prep, household errands, reminders to call my parents. I wish I could just turn it all off sometimes. I know things aren’t actually falling apart, but it’s definitely overwhelming tonight. The apartment is quiet except for the hum of the refrigerator and I can hear my partner brushing their teeth down the hall. Maybe tomorrow will be less chaotic. For now, I just want to put away this laundry and get some sleep.

Closed my laptop after yet another hour of scrolling job boards this morning, trying to decide if I’m actually looking for something stable or just torturing myself. There’s a persistent sense that I should be doing something more impressive or at least more secure, but I don’t even know what that would mean for me anymore. I thought freelancing would feel freeing, but lately it just feels like I’m drifting. The fog in my head isn’t helping, either. I keep rereading the same emails, overthinking every line before I send a response, and still worrying I sound unprofessional or unreliable. My savings are okay for now, but the anxiety about next month makes it hard to focus on the projects I do have. Sometimes I wonder if I’m cut out for this field or if there’s something fundamentally wrong with how I approach things. Other people seem to have a plan or at least some confidence, and I keep comparing myself, even though I know it’s pointless. I watched a webinar about building a personal brand and felt like I was watching someone describe an alien species. There was a moment today when I looked at the unfinished code on my screen and just felt completely detached from it, like it belonged to someone else. I know I’m supposed to push through, but the self-doubt feels heavier lately. Maybe if I broke things into smaller steps or stopped expecting everything to click instantly, I could get somewhere. For now, I just want to quiet the noise in my head long enough to get some actual work done.

I’m in the parking lot right now, trying to get my head clear before clocking in, but honestly I’m still thinking about that argument with Jenna last night. It’s not like we even meant to get into it, it started with me complaining about the schedule getting changed again, and then she got defensive, said I always make things about myself. Maybe I do, sometimes, but it’s not like I’m trying to. I just feel like I barely have room to breathe lately, with hours being cut and my rent due soon, and every little thing feels bigger than it should. I wanted to apologize but then I thought, what if she’s the one who should? But then I feel guilty for even thinking that. I know I could have just let it go instead of snapping back. My mind keeps looping around it, like maybe if I replay the conversation enough I’ll figure out what the right thing to do is. I don’t want there to be weirdness between us, especially with how much time we have to spend together at work. But also I don’t feel like I have the energy to fix everything all the time. Maybe I’ll text her later, or maybe I’ll just try to act normal and hope it passes. I wish I knew what she was thinking. Ugh, I should be focusing on work but my brain’s all foggy, and I haven’t even made it inside yet.

I’m sitting on the couch, my knee bouncing a little while I scroll through old texts from last night. There’s a weird aftertaste from the cereal I just ate, and I keep replaying the argument with Jamie in my head. It started so small: she asked if I could chip in for groceries this week, and I kind of snapped without meaning to. I know money’s tight for both of us, but I felt like she was blaming me for not pulling my weight, which sucks even if it’s not what she meant. I probably sounded defensive, talking too loud and cutting her off. She just got quiet and said she’d figure it out herself, then disappeared into her room. The silence afterward felt huge. I hate when things get like this, but my brain was all over the place, thinking about bills and the store schedule and whether I could even pick up an extra shift. Now I’m stuck here, wishing I’d handled it differently but also annoyed that I have to keep proving I’m trying. Am I overreacting, or is she just not getting how stressed I am? I keep thinking about apologizing but don’t know what words won’t come out wrong. Maybe I should just leave a note before I go to work, something simple. I don’t want this hanging over us all day, but I also feel like I’m always the one who has to fix things. Still, I miss how easy things felt between us before all this money stuff started creeping in. I wish it was just about groceries and not everything else piling up. My head feels too full to sort any of it out right now, but I know I need to do something before it gets worse.

My plate is still on the table, the fork sitting across it like I just paused for a second. I can hear the fridge humming in the background, which is about the only thing that seems steady right now. This afternoon at work was a mess of packages and instructions that got switched, so I spent an hour sorting out where a batch of shoes was actually supposed to go. No one really talked much, but I could feel there was tension. A couple of the guys were annoyed about overtime getting shuffled again, and I got stuck in the middle of it when they wanted to vent.

I tried to keep my head down and just finish what I was supposed to, but it’s hard not to feel like the new person every minute. I know people probably aren’t mad at me specifically, but I still felt awkward. It’s weird not having anyone to joke with or just eat lunch with, but maybe that will change once I’m here longer.

I’m tired, but not in a bad way. More like I used up everything I had, but I’m not upset. I’m just hoping tomorrow is a little smoother, and maybe I’ll find a way to feel more at home here.

My hands were still sticky from slicing tomatoes when I got home tonight, and all I could think about was the mess in the kitchen sink. I ended up calling Mom this morning before my shift because she left me a message saying she needed help with something at the house, but I was running late and didn’t really listen to the whole voicemail. She sounded tired on the phone, way more than usual, and I kept thinking she was about to ask for money or something I couldn’t give. I tried to keep the conversation short, but she kept circling back to Dad and how she misses him, which I never know how to handle. I wanted to say something comforting, but I was distracted, half-watching the clock and thinking about my prep list for the day. She asked if I was eating enough, which kind of pissed me off even though I know she means well. I snapped at her without meaning to, told her I had to go, and hung up. Now I keep replaying that in my head. Was I too harsh? I wish I could just be more patient, but lately, everything feels like it’s pressing in on me. Money, work, missing Dad, and trying to keep it all together. I want to call her back and apologize, but it’s late and I don’t really know what I’d say without making it weird. Maybe tomorrow I’ll feel clearer. Or maybe I’ll just keep putting it off.

Feeling a bit worn out today, mostly from juggling all the things I need to do for my parents lately and then trying to keep my own work going. I spent a chunk of the afternoon on the couch with my sketchbook in my lap, half-heartedly sketching while my mind kept drifting to the list of appointments and errands I need to schedule for Mom next week. I still haven’t gotten around to calling her doctor’s office, which I meant to do this morning, but I guess I put it off again. It’s hard to keep track of who needs what and when, especially since my brother keeps texting me about splitting up tasks but never actually follows through. I feel like I’m constantly double-checking the calendar, worried I’ll miss something or mess up the timing for their medication pickups. Meanwhile, I’ve let dishes pile up in the sink and laundry is half-finished, but I just can’t care about it right now. Socially, I keep dodging calls from a couple of friends who want to check in, but I don’t really have energy to explain everything all over again. My routine feels steady on the surface but it’s like I’m always one step behind, trying to catch up. I know this is just a phase, and things will get sorted, but right now it all feels like way too many tabs open in my brain. Maybe tomorrow I’ll finally get through my to-do list, or at least make a dent. For now, I just want to shut my eyes for a bit and not think about anything else.

The table is still cluttered with plates and my notebook. I keep glancing at tomorrow’s to-do list, trying to decide what I can move around. I booked one meeting at 10 a.m. and a product call at 2 p.m. but still nothing for Friday yet. My phone keeps buzzing with group texts about coverage for next week, but no one is confirming anything. I feel like I’m just shuffling blocks around every day, never really settling anything. There’s laundry on the chair and a stack of invoices I need to follow up on. I told myself I’d get better at this, making time for everything, but I’m not sure I am. At least I sold two sets of speakers today, which felt good. Dinner was leftovers, quick and quiet. Tomorrow I’ll try to get up early and get a head start, but right now I just want to clear the table and shut the light off.

The refrigerator hums in the background and the light coming through the window is gray, almost washed out. I keep thinking about the quick call with my brother last night. He asked if I’m settling in, whether this place feels like home yet. I said it’s fine, but that was just easier than saying I don’t know. I could hear the pause on his end, like he wanted to say more but decided not to. Maybe he thinks I should be excited about the move, or that I’m overthinking it. The boxes are mostly unpacked but my head feels cluttered, like I misplaced something important in the shuffle. I caught myself zoning out in the kitchen, thinking about how routines used to anchor me. Now I’m forcing myself to make lists: groceries, bills to update, client emails. Even simple things like finding the nearest pharmacy become small projects. It’s tiring and I’m not sure how long this phase lasts. I keep replaying the conversation, wondering if I should have just told him I feel out of place. But I didn’t want to sound like I’m complaining. There’s a practical side of me that wants to just get on with it, but another part keeps circling back to the same questions. I guess I hoped he’d say something that would make me feel less unsettled, but maybe that’s not fair. I’m not even sure what I need right now. The kitchen feels both familiar and foreign, and I can’t tell if it’s the space or just me.

I spent most of this afternoon tracking down a billing issue for a customer who was convinced we were trying to scam him. He started off pretty hostile, and for a while, it was just me repeating the same answers and feeling like we were both running in circles. I could feel my jaw getting tight, and I kept glancing at the clock, already thinking about how complicated it would be to coordinate dinner at home with my roommate later. Eventually, the customer calmed down after I managed to find a line item he hadn’t noticed. He even thanked me, which doesn’t happen as often as people think. I felt oddly relieved, but also drained, wishing I could just go somewhere quiet instead of heading back to the apartment where I know the kitchen will be a mess. This bus ride home feels like my only real alone time today. I’m restless, but also too tired to do much about it. Maybe I’ll offer to cook tonight just to avoid the awkward back-and-forth over who’s using the stove. Sometimes I wonder if I should just get my own place, but then I remember the rent. Anyway, I’m hoping tomorrow’s less of a circus, but I’m not holding my breath.

Just finished sorting through some invoices and receipts at my desk. The freelance work is trickling in but it feels like I'm always waiting to see if the next payment will cover rent or if I need to dip into savings again. On nights like this, I wonder if I'm doing the right thing staying in grad school at my age, chasing something that might not pay off, while the younger students seem to have everything figured out. 

Had another awkward dinner with L. Tried to talk about the weekend, but she seemed distracted. I wanted to bring up how stressed I've been but I could tell she wasn't up for a heavy conversation tonight. Maybe I should be better at hiding my worries, or at least not let them bleed into every conversation. It's hard to know where I fit sometimes, like I'm floating between being a student, a partner, and someone who's supposed to have it together. 

The apartment is quiet now, just the hum of my old laptop. I need to email a client back before bed, but my mind keeps circling around the same questions about the future. I wish I could just focus on one thing for a while, but that's not how life seems to work lately. At least tomorrow I only have one class to sit through. Might try to get out for a walk in the morning if it's not raining.

The hum of the fridge is the loudest thing in the apartment right now. I keep glancing at the stack of articles I still need to annotate for the research group meeting tomorrow, even though I know I’m not going to get through all of them tonight. I had planned to finish at least the methods section before dinner, but then Lila wanted to talk about some stuff that happened with her sister and we ended up in one of those conversations where neither of us really meant to sound annoyed but somehow, it just kind of built up anyway. We’re supposed to be working on communicating better but sometimes it feels like we’re both just tired and defaulting to defensiveness. I’ve got seminar notes half-finished, an email from my advisor flagged as unread, and I still haven’t put in my availability for the TA office hours next week. There’s this constant low-level pressure from deadlines I try to ignore, but it keeps resurfacing. I can’t tell if I’m actually behind or just catastrophizing, but either way, the feeling is the same. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try making an actual schedule again, though I’m skeptical it’ll stick for more than a day or two. For now, I just want to sit with the quiet and not think about the next thing for five minutes.

Walked around the block this morning to try and clear my head after another tense conversation with Sam. We barely said anything to each other before I left, but the silence felt heavier than if we’d argued. The air was crisp and I noticed a neighbor’s dog barking at a squirrel, which made me smile for a second. Still, I kept replaying last night’s disagreement about how much I’ve been around the house since losing my job. I get that the blurred lines between work and home are getting to both of us, but I can’t seem to shake this foggy feeling. I tried to focus on the rhythm of my feet on the pavement, but my mind wandered back to whether I should be doing more to help things feel normal again. Saw a couple walking and laughing and wondered if they ever argue about stupid things like who’s using the Wi-Fi too much. By the time I got home, I’d calmed down a bit, but the tension was still there, lingering. I wish I knew the right thing to say or do to make it better, but I just feel stuck. Maybe I’ll try making breakfast as a peace offering tomorrow.

Woke up to a text from my sister asking if I could help Mom with her doctor’s appointment next week, and I just stared at the phone for a while. Feels like every day lately starts with a request or a reminder or something I forgot to do, and it’s all piling up in my brain. I sat on the living room couch this morning, legs tucked under a blanket, and tried to make sense of my to-do list. I keep meaning to call the insurance company about Dad’s paperwork but I can’t seem to get past the first step. Maybe it’s just the tiredness, or maybe it’s the way the house feels emptier without him. Even the fridge seems quieter, if that makes sense.

I tried to draft an article for that food blog client but ended up staring at the blinking cursor for thirty minutes, thinking about how Mom’s been cooking less since Dad passed. Funny how grief keeps leaking into everything, even recipes. I want to be helpful, but I also feel like I’m running on fumes. The bills are scattered in a pile on the coffee table. I keep adding things to my planner and then ignoring them. Sometimes I wonder if other people are just better at handling all this, or if they’re faking it too. I keep telling myself I’ll take a walk or do something for myself, but the day slips away and I just sit here, scrolling through my phone, waiting for energy to come back.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text:
Just got on the bus after another long shift. My hands still smell faintly like grease, even though I washed them before clocking out. I kept thinking about the conversation I had with Mark during lunch. He asked me about my weekend plans and I hesitated, not sure if he was hoping I’d mention him or if he was just making small talk. I tried to joke about my idea of a good night (pizza and old movies), but he seemed distracted, like he was waiting for something else from me. 

Sitting here, watching the city slide past the window, I can’t stop replaying it. Did I come off cold? Or was he just tired too? I want to trust that this new thing between us is going somewhere, but I’m afraid of reading too much into every little exchange. Maybe I’m just exhausted, and everything feels heavier than it should. The bus is half empty tonight, which is rare, and I find myself wishing I could talk to someone who’d just tell me straight what’s next. For now, I guess I’ll just see how I feel in the morning. I really hope I didn’t mess anything up.

I remembered this morning when I left the apartment, Mom called just as I was locking the door. She asked if I’d eaten breakfast and I said yes, which wasn’t true. I hadn’t had time and didn’t want her to worry or start up about me not taking care of myself. The lie stuck with me most of the day, which is stupid. I know she just cares, but sometimes it feels like one more thing to manage. I keep thinking about how I used to brush her off a lot less, before Dad got sick last year. Everything’s been harder since then.

Now I’m on the bus home, watching the city go by. I tried to text my brother this afternoon, just to check in, but he left me on read. Not sure if I annoyed him or if he’s just busy with his own stuff. I feel restless and distracted. Tried to study during the ride but couldn’t focus. Money’s tighter than ever, and I keep going over my expenses in my head, wondering what I can cut next week. I wish I could talk to someone about all of this without it turning into a lecture or advice session. I know that’s not fair to my family, but I’m tired of pretending I’m fine when I’m not sure I am. Maybe I’ll try calling Mom back later, or maybe I’ll just tell her the truth next time.

Just finished wiping the grease off my hands, even though I’m not at the shop, the smell still lingers. I sat down at my desk this morning to look over the truck part orders for next week and realized I double-booked two jobs again. Not a huge deal but it means extra explaining to the boss, and I hate that. My partner made a joke about it while they were getting ready, and I probably got a little snappy, which I regret now. We’re trying to get better at not taking work stress out on each other. I keep meaning to write stuff down more so I can keep track but it never sticks. The shop’s been busier lately, which is good for money, just not my nerves. I’m calm now but I can tell the day’s going to be a long one. There’s a weird comfort in knowing exactly what needs fixing, even if it’s just a busted starter instead of anything bigger. I’ll try to remember to text my partner later, just to say thanks for being patient.

My car seat is still too warm from the last person who used it, and I'm sitting here in the parking lot trying to go over tonight’s checklist in my head. I have to pick up groceries after work, but I can’t remember if Mom said we needed eggs or just milk. I wrote it down somewhere, maybe in the group chat, but my phone is buried under all these bags and I’m not about to dig through everything right now. My brother texted that he’ll be home late, which means I’ll be the one getting dinner ready and making sure Grandma takes her meds on time. The house is always so crowded but somehow, it feels like I’m the only one keeping track of the little things. I’m trying to remember if I left the laundry in the dryer or if it’s still in the washer. If I don’t move it soon, someone’s going to dump it out and I’ll have to rerun it, which is always annoying. I keep thinking I should make some kind of color-coded chart for all our chores, but every time I try, someone changes their plans and it ends up a mess. Maybe I’ll just write a list on the fridge tonight and hope people actually read it. I can hear other cars pulling in, so I guess I should get going. Not looking forward to the rush tonight, but at least I remembered to bring my headphones. If nothing else, I can tune everyone out for a few minutes before dinner chaos starts.

Just turned off the TV after scrolling through my bank app again. I keep thinking if I missed some expense somewhere, but it all adds up in the worst way. I should've gone to bed earlier but my mind kept jumping to the rent payment coming up, the groceries list that keeps getting longer, and the hours I need to cover at work this week. The couch is lumpy but it feels like the only place I can just sit and try to make a list of what needs to get done tomorrow. I have to pick up my work boots from the repair shop before my shift, and I can't forget to call the internet company because the bill is showing up higher than usual. I keep telling myself to breathe and just do one thing at a time, but the next thing crowds out the last.

Tomorrow it's: check the fridge for what’s actually left, see if I can stretch what I have till payday, text my supervisor to see if I can swap a shift to Saturday. I still need to sort out laundry, and I’m almost out of detergent. Wondering if I can get away with one more load before buying more. I scribbled down a few reminders but my handwriting is a mess and I lost the sticky note somewhere in the cushions. I feel like I’m chasing my own tail with all this, but if I don’t write it down, I know I’ll forget half of it. My head feels too full but I’m still missing things, like I never actually get ahead. Maybe I’ll set an alarm early and try to get a head start, but I know I’ll be tired. Anyway, just had to get this out of my system before bed.

Tried to finalize the weekly sales numbers this morning while juggling texts with my ex about who’s picking up our son from practice tomorrow. The store was already busy by 9 a.m., and my manager wanted the new display set up before lunch. I squeezed in a call to confirm the dentist appointment I forgot to reschedule last week, but the office was closed for some staff meeting. Kept thinking I’d check our shared Google calendar on my break, but got pulled into covering another register when someone called in sick. The bus ride home now feels like the only time I can actually look at my own schedule, but the connection is spotty, so half my reminders aren’t loading. I’m tired, and it’s only Monday. At least I remembered to grab the groceries for dinner, even if I forgot the bread. There’s a half-finished to-do list in my notes app, and I keep adding more instead of crossing things off. Not sure how I’m supposed to keep track of everything when it feels like every day is just a new set of logistics to coordinate.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
I really need to figure out how to get my schedule under control. I spent half the day trying to coordinate times for tomorrow’s lab work with the lead researcher, and then realized I forgot to respond to two people about the survey project. Everything feels like it’s overlapping, and I swear I set reminders but somehow things still slip through. Maybe I just need a better system, but every time I try to set one up, I get distracted by something urgent or just lose motivation halfway through.

Tonight was supposed to be a catch-up night, but it’s almost midnight and I only finished half the reading I planned. My phone kept buzzing with Slack messages, which didn’t help. I still haven’t called my landlord about the weird noise in the bathroom pipes, and groceries are running low. I keep telling myself tomorrow will be less chaotic, but that’s what I said yesterday too. Sometimes I wonder if the stress is just because everything is new, or if I’m just not as organized as I thought. I’m tired, but my brain won’t let go of the checklist I didn’t finish.

This morning I woke up too early because I forgot to close the blinds, so the sun was basically stabbing me in the eyes at 6:15. I wandered around my new apartment in a daze, trying to find my sketchbook but I still haven’t unpacked all my art supplies. The boxes are like a maze, and I keep tripping over random stuff. I made some oatmeal but couldn’t really taste it, just kept thinking about how weird it is to start over in a new place. Everything smells different, even the water from the tap.

Now I’m in the parking lot outside work, just watching people come and go. I keep checking my phone, not really sure who I want to hear from. Maybe I’m hoping someone from my old life will message me, but they probably won’t. I’m supposed to be excited about new beginnings, but mostly I just feel floaty, like I could drift away. I keep telling myself to be patient and let things settle, but then I get fidgety and want to do a million things at once. I doodled on the back of a grocery receipt while waiting, just quick messy lines, nothing good. I don’t know if I even like my art lately. I hope I’ll figure out how to feel normal here, but right now it feels like I’m not really anywhere at all.

Feeling neutral this morning, just waiting in the car before heading in. I got here early again, which is starting to feel like a habit. I looked up from my phone and saw two classmates arguing near the entrance. It was about something small, parking spaces I think, but the way their voices carried made it sound bigger. I kept my distance, didn’t want to get pulled in, but part of me wondered if I should’ve said something to cool things down. I’m not really the type to jump into other people’s business though. It’s strange how I can be organized with my own stuff but avoid messy situations like that. I went through my notes for today’s seminar, double-checking the readings. I keep thinking if I’m being too careful, or if it’s just part of how I deal with being around people. Living alone makes it easy to not have to deal with these frictions, but every time I step out, there’s always some tension somewhere. I guess you can’t really avoid it, even if you plan your days down to the minute. The parking lot is quieter now, just a few cars rolling in. I’ll go inside soon, try to keep my head clear and focused. Sometimes I wonder if I’m missing out by not getting involved more, but I also know I like things calm. For now, I’m fine staying in my lane.

Just finished texting Alex about the kids’ pickup this weekend. It was supposed to be a quick check-in but turned into a back-and-forth about who had what going on, and suddenly I’m not even sure if I said yes to Saturday or just meant to. I kept looking at my phone, trying to keep my tone clear but not annoyed, but I think it came off short anyway. Sometimes I wish we could just use one shared calendar and be done with it, but he always says he prefers talking things through. I get it, but I don’t really want to keep explaining my work interviews or why I need to switch a day. Feels like I’m always justifying things. Maybe that’s normal for coparenting, I don’t know. 

Now it’s quiet, and I’m just eating this sandwich, kind of replaying the conversation in my head. Did I say too much? Not enough? It always feels like I’m either being too direct or too vague. Can’t tell if I’m messing things up or if this is just how it goes. I’m calm right now, not upset, but there’s that nagging feeling that I didn’t handle it perfectly again. Maybe I just care too much about keeping it smooth. Or maybe I just want to get through this job search and feel like I have things figured out for once. I don’t know, it’s hard to say.

Feeling a bit drained this afternoon but mostly just steady, trying not to let things get to me. The bus ride home gave me too much time to think about the argument I had with Alex earlier. We were supposed to figure out who was handling the grocery run and who would pick up the prescription, but it turned into this frustrating back-and-forth about who does more. I kept telling myself to stay calm, to listen, but honestly, my patience is wearing thin on these little everyday fights. I think part of it is just the weight of keeping track of every dollar, every errand, and not wanting to slip up because we really can’t afford mistakes right now.

As I sat by the window watching the city roll by, I started making mental lists of what still needs to get done tonight: study for the bio quiz, check if the rent payment actually went through, and deal with the laundry. It’s always something, always a few things left hanging. I know Alex is stressed too, so maybe I should just let tonight cool off a bit before we talk again. I wish there were more time, or maybe just a little more room in the budget so these small things didn’t feel so loaded. For now, I’ll just focus on what I can finish before bed and hope tomorrow’s a bit smoother.

persona.life_context: caring for a parent, stretched thin

journal_text: This morning I nearly tripped over Mom’s walker on my way to the kitchen; she’d left it in the middle of the hallway again. I made her oatmeal and packed my resume folder while she watched the local news. Managed to get her meds set up before I rushed out, but still forgot my own breakfast. Now I’m sitting in the car in the parking lot, ten minutes early for this temp agency intake. Sun’s out, a little glare on the dashboard. Could use a nap, honestly, but at least I remembered to bring a water bottle. It’s a lot hopping between caring for her and trying to find something steady. Just want to make it through this appointment without getting flustered.

Feeling pretty energized, but my brain is spinning a bit from today’s nonstop pace. I just had a conversation with Sam in the living room while I tried to get some work done on the couch. He brought up the overlap in our schedules again, especially around who gets the quiet time in the evenings. We both have a lot going on, but I could tell he was frustrated by how often I end up commandeering the living room for late calls. I tried to explain that I don’t always have control over when investors want to talk, but I’m not sure that landed the way I meant. There was this awkward pause where neither of us wanted to push further. I caught myself getting a bit defensive and then trying to pivot to solutions, which maybe wasn’t what he wanted right then.

I keep thinking there has to be a better way to manage our shared spaces. Maybe we need a more concrete schedule, or just to check in weekly about big stuff coming up. It’s tricky because I like things organized and predictable, but his job seems to throw curveballs too. There’s a part of me that worries I’m being too rigid, but I also can’t afford to lose focus with everything on my plate right now. Sometimes I wonder if I’m missing something obvious about how he feels.

After he went to his room, I replayed the conversation a few times in my head. I want to keep things smooth between us, but I also need to protect my work time. I guess I’ll bring it up again in a day or two, maybe after we’ve both had a chance to cool off. Honestly, living with someone while running a company isn’t as simple as I hoped, but I’m confident we’ll figure it out eventually.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text: Feeling a bit scattered this afternoon as I sit at my desk. I had every intention of getting through the edits on my novel draft, but my mind kept drifting to whether I’m actually starting to belong here. The apartment is quiet except for the occasional sound from the street, and I’m realizing how much I miss having close friends nearby. I reached out to a couple of people from last week’s writing group, but I haven’t heard back yet. Work deadlines are piling up, and sometimes it feels like I’m just treading water. I know I’m usually optimistic, and I still am, but it’s hard not to question if I made the right choice moving. At least I managed to finish two chapters, even if it took longer than planned. Maybe tomorrow will feel a little less rushed.

Just finished brushing my teeth and double-checking if my laptop charger was plugged in. It's late, everyone else is asleep, but I keep replaying the conversation I had with Dad earlier tonight at the kitchen table. He asked me again if I was sure about working on my startup instead of applying for those grad school programs. I tried to explain my reasons, the ideas that keep me up at night, but I don't think I got through to him. He nodded a lot but then brought up job security and how "everyone needs a backup plan."

I know he's just worried, but I couldn't help feeling a bit misunderstood. Maybe I wasn't as clear as I thought, or maybe he just sees risk differently. Sometimes I question whether I'm actually chasing something meaningful or if I'm just stubborn. It's hard to tell if I'm building an identity or just avoiding the paths everyone else takes. The uncertainty is heavy, but I also feel this weird optimism underneath it, like something good will come out of all this if I keep pushing.

I wish I had more privacy to think things through out loud, but that's not really possible living here. For now, I guess I'll keep my plans mostly to myself and try to figure out how to communicate them better. Maybe one day Dad will understand. Or maybe I will.

The hum of the old desk fan is louder in the mornings, or maybe I just notice it more when I’m already tired. Sunlight’s leaking through the side of the curtain, hitting the receipts I’ve stacked up to organize later. I woke up thinking about last night’s conversation with Jordan, which is an annoying way to start the day. We were supposed to be talking about work schedules and splitting bills, but it turned into this weird, passive-aggressive exchange about who’s "pulling their weight." I’m still not sure if he was actually annoyed at me or just stressed about his own money stuff. I kept trying to make a joke to lighten things up, but he barely cracked a smile. Sometimes I wonder if my humor falls flat or just gets mistaken for me not caring.

It’s hard not to take it personally, even though I know everyone’s tense right now. I replayed it in my head while brushing my teeth and kept coming back to the same question: am I being too defensive, or is he just not saying what he actually means? Maybe both. I wish I could just be straightforward with him, but I get caught up wanting to avoid conflict. The irony is, as a counselor, I’m supposed to be good at navigating this stuff, but when it’s my own life, I’m mostly just guessing. The pile of receipts is a reminder that I have enough to juggle. I’ll probably let this sit until we’re both less tired, but who knows if that’ll help or just let things fester. Feels like one thing too many today.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text:
The birds were louder than usual this morning, or maybe it just felt that way since my head was already buzzing with the day's to-do list. Walking around the block, I tried to go over my schedule in my head, but everything felt tangled. There’s a project deadline at work, and I still need to finish the assignment for my software design class. I keep forgetting if I actually replied to my professor’s email or just thought about it. My phone buzzed twice in my pocket, probably reminders I set for myself yesterday, but I ignored them. 

I feel like I’m always falling behind, even when I’m technically on track. The groceries from last night are still sitting unpacked in the hallway, and I’m not sure when I’ll find time to cook anything real. I wish I could just focus on one thing, but everything is coming at me sideways right now. Maybe after class tonight, I’ll make a new list and actually stick to it.

Just finished rinsing the dishes after dinner, but my brain is still spinning with everything that needs to get done. Today I tried to map out all the open tickets from my freelance clients, but the list just seemed to grow every time I checked my inbox. It’s like the more I try to organize, the more stuff pops up out of nowhere. There’s a deadline tomorrow I nearly forgot about, and now I’m wondering if I should pull a late night or just risk an early morning scramble. My phone kept buzzing with reminders and new requests right as I was trying to eat, and I barely tasted my food.

I keep thinking about how all this uncertainty is becoming my normal. Not knowing if I’ll have enough work next month, or if I’m even in the right line of work. Sometimes I picture myself with a steady job and a regular paycheck, but then I remember why I chose freelancing in the first place. The flexibility is nice, but I feel like I’m always on edge, waiting for the next thing to go wrong or for a gap in income to hit. It’s hard to explain to people why I stick with it when it clearly stresses me out, and honestly I’m not always sure myself.

It hit me tonight, during a rare quiet moment after dinner, that I need to find better ways to manage all this. Maybe I should set clearer boundaries with clients or at least give myself a real day off. I want to believe things will get easier if I just keep pushing, but right now it feels like I’m treading water. Hopefully tomorrow I’ll wake up with a little more clarity and less of this constant rush.

The house is so quiet right now, except for the hum of the fridge and the occasional creak from the hallway. I’m sitting at the kitchen table with my planner open and my phone buzzing every few minutes with reminders. Today felt like a mess to be honest.
