When I dropped Max off at his dad’s this morning, he clung to me so tightly and I could tell he was trying not to cry. I couldn’t really say anything to make it better, which I hate. I keep replaying it in my head, wondering if I should have lingered a little longer or tried to make him laugh before I left, but I was already late for my shift and the guilt just kept piling up all day. I know I’m supposed to have it all coordinated and be calm about the schedule, but it feels like I’m always forgetting some tiny (or huge) thing. I had to ask my coworker to swap with me next week and I could tell she was annoyed, even though she said it was fine. Maybe I’m overthinking it but I always feel like I’m asking for too much help. Tonight I keep staring at the shared calendar and the notifications and just feeling like I’m holding everything together by a thread. I keep thinking about Max’s face this morning and I don’t really know how to process it. It makes me feel sensitive and a little bit lost, honestly.

The bus is humming louder than usual tonight, or maybe I’m just more aware of it because my brain’s making its own noise. I keep thinking about the color-coded calendar on the fridge and whether I remembered to switch the laundry before leaving this morning. There’s a sticky note on my desk about the monthly meeting minutes, but I can’t remember if I emailed the final version or saved it as a draft again. I’ve got to ask Jamie if she’s taking the late shift tomorrow, since that’s going to completely throw off my plan to get groceries before the weekend. 

I should probably text my roommate to check if anyone else is using the kitchen after seven, otherwise dinner will be instant noodles again. The office coffee tasted like cardboard today, but I drank two cups out of habit. My phone keeps buzzing with calendar reminders I set for myself, but I still feel like I’m missing something important. Maybe it’s just the usual low-level panic. There’s a bag of recycling sitting by the door that’s been there for three days. I keep telling myself I’ll deal with everything when I get home, but by then, I’m exhausted and just want to put on headphones and tune everyone out. Not sure if I’d get more done if I was less scatterbrained, or if this is just how things are now.

The couch cushion is lumpy and I can feel the remote digging into my thigh, which is weirdly comforting tonight. I sat here far too long scrolling through job postings, some that seem almost made-up, like who actually hires a professional line stander or a cheese sculptor? I keep a spreadsheet of everything I apply for, color coded, but the list just grows and nothing seems to happen. My roommate came home late from her shift, tiptoeing so she wouldn’t wake me, and I pretended to be asleep because I didn’t want to explain why I was still up. I keep thinking I should be doing more, or maybe doing different things, but it’s hard to know what that looks like when every day is a mix of hope and feeling like I’m running in place. I wrote out a new schedule for tomorrow, even penciled in time for a walk, but I already feel tired imagining it. The apartment is quiet except for the hum of the fridge, and I wonder if I’m missing something everyone else figured out by this age. There’s this pressure in my chest that I can’t shake, like I’m behind, even though I know life isn’t a race. I keep telling myself I’ll look back and see this as a turning point, but right now it just feels like waiting. I wish I had some sign, or at least the energy to believe more strongly in one. Maybe tomorrow will feel different. For now, I’ll just try to get some sleep, reorganize my thoughts in the morning, and hope there’s more clarity in the daylight. 💤

Trying to figure out the best time to call Mom today, since the last few days have been a mess with her appointments and my work stuff. I ended up walking around the block this afternoon just to clear my head and maybe mentally go through the schedule again. I keep thinking I should make a shared calendar for everyone, but then I remember I’m the only one who actually checks those things. My brother texted again about helping him get to his follow-up appointment next week, which means I’ll need to shuffle two client calls and possibly reschedule that grocery delivery. It’s not that I mind, but lately it feels like every time I think I’ve got a handle on things, something else pops up, and I start worrying I’ll forget something important.

I’m still not really settled in this new place, and I keep misplacing things like my phone charger or the notebook where I jot down reminders. I caught myself making a to-do list in my head about halfway through the walk, and then realized I’d left the actual list on the kitchen table, which is just textbook me. There’s always this nagging feeling that I’m about to drop the ball on something, and I wish I could just pause everything for a day to catch up. Maybe tonight I’ll try blocking off time to actually finish some of these little tasks, but I’m already tired just thinking about it.

persona.life_context: in school, balancing work and classes

journal_text: Had to finish the mockup for the app project by midnight, which meant I was up in the kitchen late, laptop on the table and sketchbook balanced on my knee. Kept checking the time every five minutes, even though I knew it wouldn't help. The dishwasher was humming and there was this weird comfort in the routine noise, like it kept me anchored while I tried to figure out if my design choices actually looked like 'me.' I keep wondering lately what 'my style' even is, or if I’m just collecting ideas from everyone else and patching them together. School stuff feels like it’s all about learning the rules, but work wants me to break them, and I’m not sure where that leaves me. I caught myself grinning at a dumb doodle I'd made in the margin of my notes, just a little cartoon, but it felt more honest than the whole last hour of work. Maybe that's the real me? Or maybe I just like hiding behind jokes when I feel lost. I managed to submit on time, but I couldn’t shake this restless feeling, like I’m always almost catching up to myself but not quite. I want to believe there’s some moment coming where it’ll all click and I’ll know what I’m doing. For now, at least the kitchen was quiet, and I didn’t have to pretend to be super confident in front of anyone. Just me, my mess, and some leftover pasta I ate cold out of the tub. Not glamorous, but real enough.

The TV is on low in the background, but I keep getting distracted by the sound of the dryer thumping. I flopped down on the couch after my shift, shoes still on, just feeling flattened by the sheer amount of things swirling around in my head. Work was busy as usual, and I think I lifted at least a hundred boxes before lunch. My back is a little sore but nothing too bad. I texted my partner about dinner plans, and we kept missing each other's points, which was frustrating because I really am trying to get better at saying what I mean. I keep worrying I’ll mess something up, but I want us to get better at this. Still, I’m proud I spoke up instead of just letting it slide. I’m tired, but I feel like I got through another day and that’s something. Maybe after dinner we’ll sit together and actually talk, not just about work or chores, but really talk. That would be nice.

The mug in front of me is already cold, but I’m still holding it like it’s keeping my brain together. Sitting in this coffee shop corner, I’m watching people come and go while I stare at my planner, trying to figure out what I can actually get done today. I’m half-listening for my phone to buzz, expecting an email about a freelance gig that was supposed to start last week. It’s almost hilarious how every hour feels like a puzzle piece I can’t quite fit into the day.

This morning, my toddler refused to eat anything except applesauce, which meant breakfast took twice as long and we were late getting out the door. I still need to schedule her checkup, but the pediatrician’s site kept timing out, so that’s another thing for the list. Groceries are running low, especially milk, and I have no idea when I’ll get to the store between client calls and nap time. The sitter texted to say she’s not available tomorrow, which completely scrambles my plan to finish the draft for that new client.

Sometimes I feel like if I could just get an hour with no interruptions, I’d actually catch up. Instead, I’m jotting reminders on sticky notes and texting myself ideas so I don’t forget. Even though my head is spinning with logistics, I’m glad to have a quiet moment here. I just wish these little breaks lasted longer before real life pulls me back in.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
The old radiator is clicking again, keeping me company while I stare at the ceiling. I left the kitchen light on by accident, and it’s casting this weird, sharp rectangle on the living room floor. I keep thinking about the conversation I had today with a regular who asked if I was settling in. I gave my usual answer, the upbeat one, but the truth is it’s still mostly guesswork. I haven’t found a rhythm yet, and every time I think I’m getting closer, something feels off. Maybe it’s just the way everything is unfamiliar: the street names, the bus lines, even the way people pause in conversation. 

Tonight I caught myself wondering what would make this place feel like mine. Back home, I always knew what to expect, even when I didn’t like it. Here, it’s all possibility, which sounds nice until you realize it’s also a lot of uncertainty. I keep overanalyzing every small interaction, like maybe if I say the right thing or laugh at the right moment, I’ll suddenly fit in. Sometimes I feel optimistic that it’ll click eventually, but right now I’m restless, turning things over in my mind when I should be sleeping. Maybe tomorrow I’ll join that trivia night after my shift. Or maybe I’ll just go for a walk and see where I end up. Either way, I hope I start to feel a little more like myself, wherever that self is supposed to fit here.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text: This morning I remembered Mom’s voice on the phone, asking how I was sleeping lately, while I walked around the block before work. My head was foggy from staying up too late, staring at screens, but I needed the air. The sun was just coming up, not warm yet, and I kept thinking about Dad’s checkup last week. The doctor said it was nothing urgent, but I could tell from his face that he was worried. I wish I could shake the heavy feeling I get when family stuff comes up, like I’m supposed to keep everyone together but I’m not really sure how. Being with Alex is good in the sense that I can talk about it, but part of me wonders if I’m too much sometimes or if I’m saying the wrong things. We walked last night too, he listened, but I saw him check his phone twice. Maybe he’s tired too. I keep thinking about what my role is supposed to be right now, as a daughter, as someone’s partner, even just as me. The street was quiet except for a couple of dogs barking at each other. My mind kept drifting back to work deadlines and whether I’m actually doing enough. It all feels blurry together. I should’ve made breakfast before heading out but I just wanted to move, hoping the restlessness would go away. Still tired.

I just finished dinner and I'm still thinking about the text exchange with my sister earlier. She wanted to know if I could help her with some paperwork for her new apartment, but between my own assignments and remote work tasks piling up, I honestly don't know how I could fit it in. I tried to explain but I don't think I was very clear, and now I'm worried she thinks I'm just making excuses. The weirdest part is I want to help, but I feel like my brain is moving through sludge lately. I keep replaying our messages, wondering if I should have picked up the phone instead. Maybe this is just the stress talking, but it feels like every little thing is another item on a never-ending list. Is it selfish to put my own stuff first right now? I keep telling myself I'll have more clarity after the weekend, but who knows. I wish boundaries were easier to set, or that I could explain myself without sounding cold. For now, I just hope she understands, even if I barely do myself.

persona.life_context: new city, still building a social circle

journal_text:
My phone kept buzzing this afternoon, so I decided to clear my head and take a walk around the block. I needed some air and distance after that awkward text exchange with Alex. Things have been weird since last week’s group hangout, and I can’t tell if I’m overthinking it or if there’s something actually off on their end. It’s hard to read people when you’re still new in a city and everyone’s still figuring out where they fit together. 

During the walk, I replayed our conversation and tried to remember if I said anything that might have come off wrong. I know I can be too direct sometimes, but I thought I was just being honest. Part of me wants to reach out and clear the air, but the other part is just tired of initiating every repair when things go sideways. I don’t want to seem needy, but I also don’t want this to turn into something bigger than it is. It’s just exhausting trying to guess what people are really thinking.

I wish I knew if Alex was upset or just busy. Maybe everyone’s struggling to settle in, and I’m not the only one feeling out of sync. I’ll probably give it a day before texting again. For now, I just want to get through dinner without replaying the conversation for the hundredth time. The city feels bigger on days like this, but I guess that’s normal when you’re still finding your circle.

This morning I woke up to the sound of my phone alarm buzzing on the kitchen table. I guess I forgot to bring it back to my room last night, but I just let it ring while I stared at the ceiling for a bit. It took me a while to actually get out of bed and shuffle into the kitchen, and when I did, everything felt so unfamiliar again. The boxes are mostly unpacked but there’s still random stuff piled by the fridge and the mail is stacking up because I keep forgetting to change my address on things.

Mom texted me about my upcoming appointment with the new doctor here and asked if I could help her schedule Dad’s next checkup too, since she’s getting overwhelmed. I said I would, but honestly I have no idea where to even find the numbers now. My health insurance card is buried somewhere in my backpack, which I haven’t touched since moving. There’s also the thing with my sister’s school forms that need sending in, but I keep putting it off because I don’t know where to mail them from this new place. Every time I try to make a list and get organized, it just gets longer instead of shorter. 

I know I should probably eat something, but just looking at the kitchen makes me tired. I keep thinking if I can just get one thing checked off, maybe I’ll feel a bit more settled, but then another thing pops up. Still, I want to believe it’ll all feel more normal soon, even though right now it’s just a mess of reminders and half-finished chores.

The fridge hums steadily in the background while I sit at the kitchen table, leftover soup cooling in front of me. The sunlight is coming through the blinds at a sharp angle, making the dust look like glitter in the air. It’s quiet here, almost too quiet for lunch, but I guess that’s what you get when you work from home and everyone else is gone.

This morning, I got a text from my sister about Dad’s old watch. She found it in a drawer and wanted to know if I wanted it. It hit me harder than I expected. I’ve been keeping busy with work calls and fixing a stubborn generator for a client, but that message pulled me out of my routine. I keep thinking about the last time I saw him wearing it, how he used to tap the face when he was impatient. It’s strange how a little thing like a watch can open up all these memories I figured I’d shelved.

It’s been months since the funeral, but I still have moments where I expect his voice on the phone, or imagine him asking if I checked the oil in my truck. I told my sister to send me the watch, even though I’m not sure what I’ll do with it. Maybe just hold onto it for a bit. Grief sneaks up on me in small ways, and I guess today was one of those days. I’m calm now, but I know I’ll be thinking about him for the rest of the afternoon.

This morning, while brushing my teeth, I remembered the way Jamie looked at me last night when I told them I couldn’t make it to their thing because I was scheduled for another double. That face is stuck in my head. Now I’m sitting in the car, parked under this weak streetlight, trying to figure out if I should text an apology or just let it breathe. I keep checking my bank app and my work schedule, almost like one will magically relax if I stare long enough.

I know I’m not doing enough for us lately. My hours are all over the place, and when I get off, I’m just tired. There are groceries to grab, laundry piling up, and I still haven’t called the internet company like I said I would. I want to be better at all this, but it feels like I only ever have energy for one thing at a time. I keep thinking I should plan a night for us, but then I worry about overspending, so I don’t say anything. It’s just a lot to juggle, and I hope Jamie knows I’m trying. I’ll text them after my shift, I think. Maybe we can figure something out together.

Trying to remember if I actually sent that last article draft or if I just dreamed about it, because this whole remote working thing has me second-guessing my own memory. The bus was late again, so I ended up scrolling through old messages and half-finished notes, and it hit me how much of my life feels like a half-finished draft these days. I should be grateful I have work that lets me write from anywhere, but lately anywhere just means everywhere at once, and my brain feels stretched thin. Last night, after a long string of video calls that blurred together, I got a message from someone in my writing group who said they liked a poem I barely remember writing. It was nice, I guess, but I spent the rest of the ride home wondering if I even know what my voice is anymore, or if it's just this composite of deadlines, feedback, and whatever mood I happen to be in. Maybe that's dramatic, but it feels real. There was this moment on the bus, looking out at the city lights smeared by the rain, where I realized I don't remember the last time I wrote something just for myself. Everything has a purpose now, a deliverable, a client or a post. I know I'm supposed to feel accomplished or something, but mostly I just feel tired. I want to believe that I'm still a writer and not just a content machine, but it's hard to tell. Maybe tomorrow I'll set aside twenty minutes and write something pointless, just to see if it still feels good. Or maybe I'll just fall asleep and try again next week. Either way, I need to get better at drawing lines between work and living, but I'm honestly not sure how to do that yet. For now, I'm just glad the bus finally got me home.

persona.life_context: new relationship, unsure where it is going

journal_text: My legs are sticking to the plastic seat on this bus and some kid is playing a game on max volume. I keep checking my phone for a message that isn’t coming. Earlier today, I picked up groceries, got the laundry started, and tried to keep the house from looking like a toy explosion. Parenting is a lot of routine, but today my mind kept drifting to the new relationship. We had a weird conversation at lunch about where things are heading. I tried to make a joke about commitment, but it landed flat. I can’t decide if I’m reading too much into it or if things really are off. Still, I caught myself smiling at a dumb meme they sent yesterday, so I guess it’s not all bad. The calm I feel now is probably just the exhaustion talking. I’ll deal with the relationship stuff when I’m not wrangling dinner and bathtime. For now, I’m just watching the city go by and hoping the next stop is mine. I need to get home and start the next round of chores before anyone melts down.
